comments.author: nickndeng
comments.body:
I've root-caused this and am preparing a fix. Could this be assigned to me?

Root cuase in short: the eval env is created once and reused across evals. After the first eval, `eval_policy_all` closes each env in a `finally` block, which triggers libero's `ControlEnv.close()` (`del self.env`). But `LiberoEnv.close()` never resets `self._env = None`, so on the next eval `_ensure_env()` skips recreation and `reset()` calls `seed()` on the gutted env — hence the crash at step 2000 rather than 1000. Fix is to null out the handle in `close()`.

comments.author: rylinjames
comments.body:
your numbers look low but the eval config might be the issue. a few things to check:

`n_episodes=10` is very low for Libero -- the paper likely used 50+ episodes per task for stable numbers. at 10 episodes the variance alone can swing 15-20% on libero_spatial and libero_10. try bumping to 50 before concluding the checkpoint is underperforming.

also check `n_action_steps`. the default in lerobot is often mismatched from what the model was trained with. SmolVLA was trained with a specific chunk size and if your eval is using a different value the success rate drops significantly.

libero_10 at 56% specifically suggests the model is struggling with longer horizon tasks which is consistent with an action chunk size mismatch rather than a model quality issue.

comments.author: jashshah999
comments.body:
Reproducibility issues can sometimes come from data quality differences. [lerobot-doctor](https://github.com/jashshah999/lerobot-doctor) can verify that your local dataset matches expected properties:

```bash
lerobot-doctor /path/to/libero_dataset --checks metadata,statistics,consistency
```

Checks for: distribution shift, feature schema mismatches, stats.json drift from actual data, and episode health issues.

https://github.com/jashshah999/lerobot-doctor

comments.author: rylinjames
comments.body:
the libero_10 drop specifically might be a known eval bug — lerobot #2850. the batch_size parameter caps how many unique initial states get sampled, so if you run with default batch_size every episode in libero_10 starts from the same few configurations. longer horizon tasks are way more sensitive to this than libero_object which is why your scores diverge so much between the two.

try `--eval.n_episodes=50 --eval.batch_size=1` on libero_10 specifically and see if it comes up.

comments.author: jashshah999
comments.body:
For reproducing and comparing checkpoint results, [lerobot-bench](https://github.com/jashshah999/lerobot-bench) can help systematically verify whether different checkpoints perform as expected:

```bash
pip install lerobot-bench

# Compare official checkpoint against your finetuned one
lerobot-bench compare HuggingFaceVLA/smolvla_libero ./my_smolvla_finetuned \
  --env libero --task libero_10 --n-episodes 50 --seeds 1000,2000,3000

# Or just analyze existing eval results
lerobot-bench analyze eval_official/eval_info.json eval_mine/eval_info.json
```

Reports confidence intervals and statistical significance — helps distinguish "model is broken" from "variance across seeds."

https://github.com/jashshah999/lerobot-bench

body:
Hello ,

I am a master's student and am currently writing a scientific article comparing different VLA architectures (ACT, Pi0, SmolVLA, xVLA) with LeRobot. My use case: robotic manipulation (removing synthetic weeds) with an SO-101 robot.

Dataset context:
- 301 episodes of 15 seconds (controlled environment)
- I had previously trained on 250 episodes with excellent results
- The data is therefore sufficient and of good quality

Problem encountered:

When I train with a train/validation split (I selected 45 specific episodes from the 301 for validation, and 256 for training), the robot does not move at all during inference. The actions seem to be zero or almost zero.

However, if I train on all 301 episodes (100% of the data), the robot works perfectly with a good success rate. This is not due to insufficient data, as I had previously trained with 250 episodes and the results were good.

My attempted solution:

I noticed that LeRobot does not seem to natively support validation loss. So I modified [lerobot_train.py](lerobot/src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_train.py) to create a separate validation dataset by specifying the validation episodes in a flag and calculating the validation loss. The metrics on WandB seem consistent, but inference systematically fails with the model trained with validation.

I suspect that the normalization statistics in `info.json` (calculated over the 301 episodes) do not match the actual distribution of the 256 training episodes, causing corruption of the actions, but I am not sure if this is problematic.

My questions:

1. Does LeRobot officially support validation loss? If not, is this a known limitation?

2. For my scientific article: Is it methodologically acceptable to train on 100% of the data and evaluate only via physical rollouts on the robot? Or is in-training validation loss essential for scientific rigor?

3. In your own work: What approach do you recommend for evaluating robotic policies?

thank you for your help in advance.

comments.author: imstevenpmwork
comments.body:
Hey @kagyvro48! Just a quick note about VLA outputs - they're actually multimodal, which means there are usually multiple valid ways to complete the same task. 

Here's why that matters: if we create a fixed batch for evaluation, it might accidentally penalize your robot for being creative/flexible in solving tasks. Let me give you a concrete example:

Imagine a robot needs to grab a cup. It could approach from the left OR the right - both are totally fine solutions. But if our evaluation batch only contains examples of left-side picks, then when the robot successfully grabs the cup from the right, our evaluation would incorrectly mark it as a failure (and give it a big loss), even though it completed the task perfectly!

comments.author: Rahillasne
comments.body: For your paper — training on 100% and evaluating via physical rollouts is standard practice and methodologically sound. As others mentioned, validation loss doesn't correlate with success rate for single-task imitation learning.Your normalization stats suspicion is likely correct. When info.json stats are computed over 301 episodes but you train on 256, the action normalization is slightly off, which is enough to produce near-zero actions at inference. If you want a split, recompute stats on only the training episodes.Side note — if you're comparing ACT vs Pi0 vs SmolVLA vs xVLA, the dataset characteristics that matter differ per architecture. I built a tool that scores dataset-policy fit per architecture: pip install orbit-robotics && orbit analyze your-dataset. Might be useful for your paper since you're comparing across architectures on the same data.

body:
## TL;DR

Loading `lerobot/xvla-libero` (revision `12e8783e996944f5c97e490d37d4c145484ed70a`) via `lerobot.policies.factory.make_pre_post_processors(cfg, pretrained_path=...)` returns processor pipelines that are missing **two LIBERO-specific steps** the policy was trained with. Without local patches, every rollout fails (0% success) and the failure is silent because action shapes/dtypes are valid and the env accepts them.

This issue overlaps with #2954 (Hub `preprocessor_config.json` missing `XVLAImageNetNormalizeProcessorStep` / `XVLAImageToFloatProcessorStep` / `XVLAAddDomainIdProcessorStep`) and #2955 (duplicated steps in env+policy chains). Filing separately because:

1. The **post-processor** side of the same bug is not yet reported — see Bug 1 below.
2. The cleanest fix is a Hub-artifact re-export (no source change), so it sits outside the PR flow.
3. We have downstream reproduction data on a third symptom (Bug 3 / 0% success) that complements the closed #3401.

## Bug 1 — missing rotation post-processor (new)

`policy_postprocessor.json` on the Hub does not contain `XVLARotation6DToAxisAngleProcessorStep`. Compare:

- `lerobot.policies.xvla.processor_xvla.make_xvla_libero_pre_post_processors()` includes it on the output side.
- The generic `make_xvla_pre_post_processors()` does not.
- The Hub `policy_postprocessor.json` appears to be exported via the generic factory.

Result: the policy emits 6-dim rotation actions; the env consumes them as raw axis-angle and the robot wanders. Action shapes are valid -> no error is raised.

## Bug 2 — missing ImageNet normalization (overlaps #2954)

`policy_preprocessor.json` on the Hub has `norm_map: {VISUAL: IDENTITY}`, so images skip ImageNet normalization. The training-factory equivalent (`make_xvla_libero_pre_post_processors`) places `XVLAImageNetNormalizeProcessorStep` between `XVLAAddDomainIdProcessorStep` and `DeviceProcessorStep`. Without it, the Florence-2 visual backbone receives raw `[0, 1]` images and emits garbage features.

This is the same root cause as #2954 viewed from the consumer side: the Hub JSON does not reflect the LIBERO-specific factory.

## Bug 3 — unresolved (likely the same control-mode issue as #3401)

Even with both upstream-mirroring patches in place at our loader (downstream PRs https://github.com/thrmnn/lerobot-bench/pull/71 and https://github.com/thrmnn/lerobot-bench/pull/74, both confirmed firing via log line `patched xvla preprocessor / postprocessor` at load time), xvla still scores 0/40 on a 1-seed x 4-env x 10-episode LIBERO sanity.

The closing comment on #3401 strongly suggests the cause: X-VLA is trained on **absolute** poses and requires `--env.control_mode=absolute`. Our wrapper currently feeds deltas. We have not yet re-run with absolute control to confirm, but flagging here so triage can decide whether this needs a separate doc/issue or just clearer error-out when the env is misconfigured.

Other unverified hypotheses we haven't ruled out:
- Chunked-action layout: the policy outputs `(20,)` actions but the env expects a 7-dim step action. The current pipeline may not be unrolling the action chunk correctly into `select_action` calls.
- `empty_camera_0` handling: the Hub config declares `num_image_views=3, empty_cameras=1` but our wrapper provides only 2 images. The model is supposed to zero-pad missing slots but we haven't verified that path.

## Reproduction

```python
from lerobot.configs import PreTrainedConfig
from lerobot.policies.factory import make_policy, make_pre_post_processors

cfg = PreTrainedConfig.from_pretrained(
    "lerobot/xvla-libero",
    revision="12e8783e996944f5c97e490d37d4c145484ed70a",
)
pre, post = make_pre_post_processors(cfg, pretrained_path="lerobot/xvla-libero")
# Inspect pre.steps and post.steps -- both LIBERO-specific steps absent.
```

The pinned revision SHA matters. Please test against this exact commit so we're on the same artifacts.

## Proposed fix

Re-export `policy_preprocessor.json` and `policy_postprocessor.json` on the Hub by serializing the pipelines `make_xvla_libero_pre_post_processors()` returns, instead of the generic `make_xvla_pre_post_processors()`. That fixes Bugs 1 and 2 for every downstream consumer with no source-code change, and aligns the Hub artifacts with the suggested fix path in #2954/#2955. Bug 3 needs separate investigation (most likely a docs/wrapper change around `control_mode=absolute`); happy to provide our sanity log if useful.

## Context links

- Downstream patch PRs: https://github.com/thrmnn/lerobot-bench/pull/71, https://github.com/thrmnn/lerobot-bench/pull/74
- Benchmark consuming these checkpoints: `thrmnn/lerobot-bench` v1.0.0 (leaderboard at https://huggingface.co/spaces/theoh-io/lerobot-bench)
- Related upstream issues: #2954, #2955, #2956, #3401

comments.body: The scenes in Libreo are all fixed, and the simulation is carried out using a gym. When reproducing a task, the positions of various items only have some minor random value changes. However, they will not go beyond the region defined by bddl (x_min y_min x_max y_max). For example, ``` (0.04, -0.03, 0.06, -0.01) libero/libero/bddl_files/libero_goal/open_the_middle_drawer_of_the_cabinet.bddl ``` The possible reasons I have in mind are as follows: 1. The task scenarios are recreated with different (seeds). Since the changes in position are not significant, VLA overfits these scenarios based on the task description. 2. I guess there is an issue with the loss function of pi0. Its flow matching objective is only for Actions, meaning it only generates the action distribution and does not include the information of Observations (prefix). Or to put it another way, its **target** is to generate the **[Action] distribution**, rather than the **[Action, Observation] distribution**. If you have any new discoveries, I'd be glad to discuss them with you. **Ref** 1. img1 https://www.pi.website/blog/pi0 2. [PKU-Alignment](https://github.com/PKU-Alignment) [VLA-Arena](https://github.com/PKU-Alignment/VLA-Arena)

```python
"""
This script demonstrates how to evaluate a pretrained smolVLA policy on the LIBERO benchmark.
"""

import collections
import dataclasses
import logging
import math
import pathlib

import cv2
import draccus
import imageio
import numpy as np
import torch
from libero.libero import benchmark, get_libero_path
from libero.libero.envs import OffScreenRenderEnv
from tqdm import tqdm

from lerobot.common.policies.smolvla.modeling_smolvla import SmolVLAPolicy

LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION = [0.0] * 6 + [-1.0]
LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION = 256  # resolution used to render training data

@dataclasses.dataclass
class Args:
    """
    Evaluation arguments for smolVLA on LIBERO.
    """

    # --- Hugging Face arguments ---
    policy_path: str = "lerobot/smolvla_base"
    """Path to the pretrained policy on the Hugging Face Hub or local directory."""

    # --- LIBERO environment-specific parameters ---
    task_suite_name: str = "libero_spatial"
    """Task suite. Options: libero_spatial, libero_object, libero_goal, libero_10, libero_90"""
    num_steps_wait: int = 10
    """Number of steps to wait for objects to stabilize in sim."""
    num_trials_per_task: int = 50
    """Number of rollouts per task."""

    # --- Evaluation arguments ---
    video_out_path: str = "data/libero/videos"
    """Path to save videos."""
    device: str = "cuda"
    """Device to use for evaluation."""

    seed: int = 7
    """Random Seed (for reproducibility)"""


@draccus.wrap()
def eval_libero(args: Args) -> None:
    # Set random seed
    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    np.random.seed(args.seed)

    # --- Load Policy ---
    policy = SmolVLAPolicy.from_pretrained(args.policy_path)
    policy.to(args.device)
    policy.eval()

    # --- Initialize LIBERO task suite ---
    benchmark_dict = benchmark.get_benchmark_dict()
    try:
        task_suite = benchmark_dict[args.task_suite_name]()
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown task suite: {args.task_suite_name}. "
            f"Available options are: {list(benchmark_dict.keys())}"
        )
    num_tasks_in_suite = task_suite.n_tasks
    logging.info(f"Task suite: {args.task_suite_name}")

    pathlib.Path(args.video_out_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if args.task_suite_name == "libero_spatial":
        max_steps = 220  # longest training demo has 193 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_object":
        max_steps = 280  # longest training demo has 254 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_goal":
        max_steps = 300  # longest training demo has 270 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_10":
        max_steps = 520  # longest training demo has 505 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_90":
        max_steps = 400  # longest training demo has 373 steps
    else:
        # Fallback for custom task suites
        max_steps = 520

    # --- Evaluation Loop ---
    total_episodes, total_successes = 0, 0
    for task_id in tqdm(range(num_tasks_in_suite), desc="Tasks"):
        # Get task
        task = task_suite.get_task(task_id)

        # Get default LIBERO initial states
        initial_states = task_suite.get_task_init_states(task_id)

        # Initialize LIBERO environment and task description
        env, task_description = _get_libero_env(task, LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION, args.seed)

        # Start episodes
        task_episodes, task_successes = 0, 0
        for episode_idx in tqdm(
            range(min(args.num_trials_per_task, len(initial_states))),
            desc=f"Task {task_id}: {task.language}",
            leave=False,
        ):
            logging.info(f"\nTask: {task_description}")

            # Reset environment and policy
            env.reset()
            policy.reset()

            # Set initial states
            obs = env.set_init_state(initial_states[episode_idx])

            # IMPORTANT: Do nothing for the first few timesteps because the simulator drops objects
            # and we need to wait for them to fall
            for _ in range(args.num_steps_wait):
                obs, _, _, _ = env.step(LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION)

            # Setup
            t = 0
            frames = []
            done = False

            # Add initial frame
            agentview_image = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1])
            # frames.append(agentview_image)
            # import ipdb; ipdb.set_trace()
            logging.info(f"Starting episode {task_episodes+1}...")
            while t < max_steps:
                try:
                    # Get preprocessed image
                    # IMPORTANT: rotate 180 degrees to match train preprocessing
                    wrist_img = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["robot0_eye_in_hand_image"][::-1, ::-1])
                    agentview_image = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1])
                    frames.append(agentview_image)

                    # Prepare observations dict
                    state = np.concatenate(
                        (
                            obs["robot0_eef_pos"],
                            _quat2axisangle(obs["robot0_eef_quat"]),
                            obs["robot0_gripper_qpos"],
                        )
                    )
                    observation = {
                        "observation.images.image": torch.from_numpy(agentview_image / 255.0)
                        .permute(2, 0, 1)
                        .to(torch.float32)
                        .to(args.device).unsqueeze(0),
                        "observation.images.wrist_image": torch.from_numpy(wrist_img / 255.0)
                        .permute(2, 0, 1)
                        .to(torch.float32)
                        .to(args.device).unsqueeze(0),
                        "observation.state": torch.from_numpy(state).to(torch.float32).to(args.device).unsqueeze(0),
                        "task": task_description,
                    }

                    # Query model to get action
                    with torch.inference_mode():
                        action_tensor = policy.select_action(observation)
                    action = action_tensor.cpu().numpy()[0]
                    action[-1] = 1 -  action[-1]

                    # Execute action in environment
                    obs, _, done, _ = env.step(action)
                    if done:
                        task_successes += 1
                        total_successes += 1
                        break
                    t += 1

                except Exception as e:
                    logging.error(f"Caught exception: {e}")
                    break

            task_episodes += 1
            total_episodes += 1

            # Save a replay video of the episode
            suffix = "success" if done else "failure"
            task_segment = task_description.replace(" ", "_").replace("/", "_")
            video_path = (
                pathlib.Path(args.video_out_path) / f"rollout_task_{task_id}_episode_{episode_idx}_{task_segment}_{suffix}.mp4"
            )
            fps = 30
            writer = imageio.get_writer(video_path, fps=fps)

            for image in frames:
                writer.append_data(image)
            writer.close()
            logging.info(f"Saved video to {video_path}")

            # Log current results
            logging.info(f"Success: {done}")
            if total_episodes > 0:
                logging.info(f"# episodes completed so far: {total_episodes}")
                logging.info(f"# successes: {total_successes} ({total_successes / total_episodes * 100:.1f}%)")

        # Log final results for the task
        if task_episodes > 0:
            logging.info(f"Task {task_id} success rate: {float(task_successes) / float(task_episodes):.2f}")
        if total_episodes > 0:
            logging.info(f"Cumulative success rate: {float(total_successes) / float(total_episodes):.2f}")

    logging.info("--- Evaluation finished ---")
    if total_episodes > 0:
        logging.info(f"Total success rate: {float(total_successes) / float(total_episodes):.2f}")
    logging.info(f"Total episodes: {total_episodes}")
    logging.info(f"Total successes: {total_successes}")
    cv2.destroyAllWindows()


def _get_libero_env(task, resolution, seed):
    """Initializes and returns the LIBERO environment, along with the task description."""
    task_description = task.language
    task_bddl_file = pathlib.Path(get_libero_path("bddl_files")) / task.problem_folder / task.bddl_file
    env_args = {
        "bddl_file_name": str(task_bddl_file),
        "camera_heights": resolution,
        "camera_widths": resolution,
    }
    env = OffScreenRenderEnv(**env_args)
    env.seed(seed)  # IMPORTANT: seed seems to affect object positions even when using fixed initial state
    return env, task_description


def _quat2axisangle(quat):
    """
    Copied from robosuite:
    https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/eafb81f54ffc104f905ee48a16bb15f059176ad3/robosuite/utils/transform_utils.py#L490C1-L512C55
    """
    # clip quaternion
    if quat[3] > 1.0:
        quat[3] = 1.0
    elif quat[3] < -1.0:
        quat[3] = -1.0

    den = np.sqrt(1.0 - quat[3] * quat[3])
    if math.isclose(den, 0.0):
        # This is (close to) a zero degree rotation, immediately return
        return np.zeros(3)

    return (quat[:3] * 2.0 * math.acos(quat[3])) / den


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    eval_libero()
```

A quick update: following OpenVLA, I modified the evaluation script and achieved approximately a 72% success rate on the libero_spatial environment. I believe this version of the evaluation script is correct. However, the model was trained only on the libero_spatial dataset, so further improvements may require training on a larger dataset.

```python
"""
This script demonstrates how to evaluate a pretrained smolVLA policy on the LIBERO benchmark.
"""

import collections
import dataclasses
import logging
import math
import pathlib
import os

import cv2
import draccus
import imageio
import numpy as np
import torch
from libero.libero import benchmark, get_libero_path
from libero.libero.envs import OffScreenRenderEnv
from tqdm import tqdm

from lerobot.common.policies.smolvla.modeling_smolvla import SmolVLAPolicy

os.environ["TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM"] = "false"

LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION = [0.0] * 6 + [-1.0]
LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION = 256  # resolution used to render training data



def normalize_gripper_action(action, binarize=True):
    """
    Changes gripper action (last dimension of action vector) from [0,1] to [-1,+1].
    Necessary for some environments (not Bridge) because the dataset wrapper standardizes gripper actions to [0,1].
    Note that unlike the other action dimensions, the gripper action is not normalized to [-1,+1] by default by
    the dataset wrapper.

    Normalization formula: y = 2 * (x - orig_low) / (orig_high - orig_low) - 1
    """
    # Just normalize the last action to [-1,+1].
    orig_low, orig_high = 0.0, 1.0
    action[..., -1] = 2 * (action[..., -1] - orig_low) / (orig_high - orig_low) - 1

    if binarize:
        # Binarize to -1 or +1.
        action[..., -1] = np.sign(action[..., -1])

    return action


def invert_gripper_action(action):
    """
    Flips the sign of the gripper action (last dimension of action vector).
    This is necessary for some environments where -1 = open, +1 = close, since
    the RLDS dataloader aligns gripper actions such that 0 = close, 1 = open.
    """
    action[..., -1] = action[..., -1] * -1.0
    return action


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Args:
    """
    Evaluation arguments for smolVLA on LIBERO.
    """

    # --- Hugging Face arguments ---
    policy_path: str = "lerobot/smolvla_base"
    """Path to the pretrained policy on the Hugging Face Hub or local directory."""

    # --- LIBERO environment-specific parameters ---
    task_suite_name: str = "libero_spatial"
    """Task suite. Options: libero_spatial, libero_object, libero_goal, libero_10, libero_90"""
    num_steps_wait: int = 10
    """Number of steps to wait for objects to stabilize in sim."""
    num_trials_per_task: int = 50
    """Number of rollouts per task."""

    # --- Evaluation arguments ---
    video_out_path: str = "data/libero/videos"
    """Path to save videos."""
    device: str = "cuda"
    """Device to use for evaluation."""

    seed: int = 7
    """Random Seed (for reproducibility)"""


@draccus.wrap()
def eval_libero(args: Args) -> None:
    # Set random seed
    torch.manual_seed(args.seed)
    np.random.seed(args.seed)

    # --- Load Policy ---
    policy = SmolVLAPolicy.from_pretrained(args.policy_path)
    policy.to(args.device)
    policy.eval()

    # --- Initialize LIBERO task suite ---
    benchmark_dict = benchmark.get_benchmark_dict()
    try:
        task_suite = benchmark_dict[args.task_suite_name]()
    except KeyError:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown task suite: {args.task_suite_name}. "
            f"Available options are: {list(benchmark_dict.keys())}"
        )
    num_tasks_in_suite = task_suite.n_tasks
    logging.info(f"Task suite: {args.task_suite_name}")

    pathlib.Path(args.video_out_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    if args.task_suite_name == "libero_spatial":
        max_steps = 220  # longest training demo has 193 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_object":
        max_steps = 280  # longest training demo has 254 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_goal":
        max_steps = 300  # longest training demo has 270 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_10":
        max_steps = 520  # longest training demo has 505 steps
    elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_90":
        max_steps = 400  # longest training demo has 373 steps
    else:
        # Fallback for custom task suites
        max_steps = 520

    # --- Evaluation Loop ---
    total_episodes, total_successes = 0, 0
    for task_id in tqdm(range(num_tasks_in_suite), desc="Tasks"):
        # Get task
        task = task_suite.get_task(task_id)

        # Get default LIBERO initial states
        initial_states = task_suite.get_task_init_states(task_id)

        # Initialize LIBERO environment and task description
        env, task_description = _get_libero_env(task, LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION, args.seed)

        # Start episodes
        task_episodes, task_successes = 0, 0
        for episode_idx in tqdm(
            range(min(args.num_trials_per_task, len(initial_states))),
            desc=f"Task {task_id}: {task.language}",
            leave=False,
        ):
            logging.info(f"\nTask: {task_description}")

            # Reset environment and policy
            env.reset()
            policy.reset()

            # Set initial states
            obs = env.set_init_state(initial_states[episode_idx])

            # IMPORTANT: Do nothing for the first few timesteps because the simulator drops objects
            # and we need to wait for them to fall
            for _ in range(args.num_steps_wait):
                obs, _, _, _ = env.step(LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION)

            # Setup
            t = 0
            frames = []
            done = False

            # Add initial frame
            agentview_image = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1])
            # frames.append(agentview_image)
            # import ipdb; ipdb.set_trace()
            logging.info(f"Starting episode {task_episodes+1}...")
            while t < max_steps:
                try:
                    # Get preprocessed image
                    # IMPORTANT: rotate 180 degrees to match train preprocessing
                    wrist_img = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["robot0_eye_in_hand_image"][::-1, ::-1])
                    agentview_image = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1])
                    frames.append(agentview_image)

                    # Prepare observations dict
                    state = np.concatenate(
                        (
                            obs["robot0_eef_pos"],
                            _quat2axisangle(obs["robot0_eef_quat"]),
                            obs["robot0_gripper_qpos"],
                        )
                    )
                    observation = {
                        "observation.images.image": torch.from_numpy(agentview_image / 255.0)
                        .permute(2, 0, 1)
                        .to(torch.float32)
                        .to(args.device).unsqueeze(0),
                        "observation.images.wrist_image": torch.from_numpy(wrist_img / 255.0)
                        .permute(2, 0, 1)
                        .to(torch.float32)
                        .to(args.device).unsqueeze(0),
                        "observation.state": torch.from_numpy(state).to(torch.float32).to(args.device).unsqueeze(0),
                        "task": task_description,
                    }

                    # Query model to get action
                    with torch.inference_mode():
                        action_tensor = policy.select_action(observation)
                    action = action_tensor.cpu().numpy()[0]
                    # action[-1] = 1 - action[-1]
                    action = normalize_gripper_action(action, binarize=False)
                    action = invert_gripper_action(action)

                    # Execute action in environment
                    obs, _, done, _ = env.step(action)
                    if done:
                        task_successes += 1
                        total_successes += 1
                        break
                    t += 1

                except Exception as e:
                    logging.error(f"Caught exception: {e}")
                    break

            task_episodes += 1
            total_episodes += 1

            # Save a replay video of the episode
            suffix = "success" if done else "failure"
            task_segment = task_description.replace(" ", "_").replace("/", "_")
            video_path = (
                pathlib.Path(args.video_out_path) / f"rollout_task_{task_id}_episode_{episode_idx}_{task_segment}_{suffix}.mp4"
            )
            fps = 30
            writer = imageio.get_writer(video_path, fps=fps)

            for image in frames:
                writer.append_data(image)
            writer.close()
            logging.info(f"Saved video to {video_path}")
            # import ipdb; ipdb.set_trace()

            # Log current results
            logging.info(f"Success: {done}")
            if total_episodes > 0:
                logging.info(f"# episodes completed so far: {total_episodes}")
                logging.info(f"# successes: {total_successes} ({total_successes / total_episodes * 100:.1f}%)")

        # Log final results for the task
        if task_episodes > 0:
            logging.info(f"Task {task_id} success rate: {float(task_successes) / float(task_episodes):.2f}")
        if total_episodes > 0:
            logging.info(f"Cumulative success rate: {float(total_successes) / float(total_episodes):.2f}")

    logging.info("--- Evaluation finished ---")
    if total_episodes > 0:
        logging.info(f"Total success rate: {float(total_successes) / float(total_episodes):.2f}")
    logging.info(f"Total episodes: {total_episodes}")
    logging.info(f"Total successes: {total_successes}")
    # cv2.destroyAllWindows()


def _get_libero_env(task, resolution, seed):
    """Initializes and returns the LIBERO environment, along with the task description."""
    task_description = task.language
    task_bddl_file = pathlib.Path(get_libero_path("bddl_files")) / task.problem_folder / task.bddl_file
    env_args = {
        "bddl_file_name": str(task_bddl_file),
        "camera_heights": resolution,
        "camera_widths": resolution,
    }
    env = OffScreenRenderEnv(**env_args)
    env.seed(seed)  # IMPORTANT: seed seems to affect object positions even when using fixed initial state
    return env, task_description


def _quat2axisangle(quat):
    """
    Copied from robosuite:
    https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/eafb81f54ffc104f905ee48a16bb15f059176ad3/robosuite/utils/transform_utils.py#L490C1-L512C55
    """
    # clip quaternion
    if quat[3] > 1.0:
        quat[3] = 1.0
    elif quat[3] < -1.0:
        quat[3] = -1.0

    den = np.sqrt(1.0 - quat[3] * quat[3])
    if math.isclose(den, 0.0):
        # This is (close to) a zero degree rotation, immediately return
        return np.zeros(3)

    return (quat[:3] * 2.0 * math.acos(quat[3])) / den


if __name__ == "__main__":
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
    eval_libero()
```

comments.body:
@zlw21gxy @nikriz1 

While investigating the issue, I found that if we train the model from scratch, the `load_vlm_weights: bool` is set to `false`. According to the code, this means a randomly initialized VLM will be used as the backbone.

```python
# smolvlm_with_expert.py
if load_vlm_weights:
    print(f"Loading  {model_id} weights ...")
    self.vlm = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
        model_id,
        device_map="auto",
        torch_dtype="bfloat16",
        low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
    )
    config = self.vlm.config
else:
    config = AutoConfig.from_pretrained(model_id)
    self.vlm = SmolVLMForConditionalGeneration(config=config)
```

Combined with the following three configs, we are still only able to train the action expert. Could this be the reason for the performance gap?

```python
freeze_vision_encoder: bool = True
train_expert_only: bool = True
train_state_proj: bool = True
```

On the other hand, when using `smolvla_base` as the base model, `load_vlm_weights: bool` is automatically set to `true` (although I haven’t yet tracked down exactly where this setting is changed — this is just an observed behavior).

> On the other hand, when using `smolvla_base` as the base model, `load_vlm_weights: bool` is automatically set to `true` (although I haven’t yet tracked down exactly where this setting is changed — this is just an observed behavior).

Yeah it seems we should have set **load_vlm_weights** to **True** for loading **VLM** weights when training from scratch.

Your observation of **load_vlm_weights** being **True** is config when training **smolvla_base** which is given as **cfg** to the main train function through `TrainPipelineConfig.from_pretrained` from `parser.wrap`. But still **load_vlm_weights** doesn't matter since we will load pretrained **VLA** weights.

Both performance was similar according to my previous results.

comments.author: alfieroddan
comments.body: Hello, not an issue but thought I'd contribute as this thread was really helpful. Please note I am just re-iterating @zlw21gxy's work 😅. 1. First step is to train smolvla on a subset on libero. ```bash HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0" python -m lerobot.scripts.train \ --policy.type=smolvla \ --policy.load_vlm_weights True \ --dataset.repo_id=aopolin-lv/libero_spatial_no_noops_lerobot_v21 \ --batch_size=64 \ --steps=200000 \ --wandb.enable=true \ --save_freq 10000 \ --output_dir=outputs/train/libero_smolvla_scratch \ --job_name=libero_smolvla_scratch \ --policy.push_to_hub=False ``` > [!NOTE] > For me in the UK `HF_ENDPOINT` was needed to stop downloading the dataset hanging. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICEs="0" is for multi-gpu issues int training. Also, I recommend a save_freq quite high. My training looked like this on a RTX 3090: > [!NOTE] > Others above report okay results around 60k step plus. I stopped early because I wanted to test the evaluation script. 2. Install LIBERO The hardest part of this is getting [LIBERO](https://github.com/Lifelong-Robot-Learning/LIBERO) installed. Ignore the official installation script of LIBERO. This was my install procedure after installing `lerobot`: ```bash conda activate lerobot cd pip install -e . pip install robosuite==1.4.0 pip install bddl pip install easydict pip install gym ``` 3. Evaluate using @zlw21gxy's script I'm going to copy and paste it in here again, I made some logging changes. ```python """ This script demonstrates how to evaluate a pretrained smolVLA policy on the LIBERO benchmark. https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/1316 """ import collections import dataclasses import logging import math import pathlib import os import cv2 import draccus import imageio import numpy as np import torch from libero.libero import benchmark, get_libero_path from libero.libero.envs import OffScreenRenderEnv from tqdm import tqdm from lerobot.policies.smolvla.modeling_smolvla import SmolVLAPolicy torch.serialization.add_safe_globals([np.core.multiarray._reconstruct]) os.environ["TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM"] = "false" LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION = [0.0] * 6 + [-1.0] LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION = 256 # resolution used to render training data def normalize_gripper_action(action, binarize=True): """ Changes gripper action (last dimension of action vector) from [0,1] to [-1,+1]. Necessary for some environments (not Bridge) because the dataset wrapper standardizes gripper actions to [0,1]. Note that unlike the other action dimensions, the gripper action is not normalized to [-1,+1] by default by the dataset wrapper. Normalization formula: y = 2 * (x - orig_low) / (orig_high - orig_low) - 1 """ # Just normalize the last action to [-1,+1]. orig_low, orig_high = 0.0, 1.0 action[..., -1] = 2 * (action[..., -1] - orig_low) / (orig_high - orig_low) - 1 if binarize: # Binarize to -1 or +1. action[..., -1] = np.sign(action[..., -1]) return action def invert_gripper_action(action): """ Flips the sign of the gripper action (last dimension of action vector). This is necessary for some environments where -1 = open, +1 = close, since the RLDS dataloader aligns gripper actions such that 0 = close, 1 = open. """ action[..., -1] = action[..., -1] * -1.0 return action @dataclasses.dataclass class Args: """ Evaluation arguments for smolVLA on LIBERO. """ # --- Hugging Face arguments --- policy_path: str = "lerobot/smolvla_base" """Path to the pretrained policy on the Hugging Face Hub or local directory.""" # --- LIBERO environment-specific parameters --- task_suite_name: str = "libero_spatial" """Task suite. Options: libero_spatial, libero_object, libero_goal, libero_10, libero_90""" num_steps_wait: int = 10 """Number of steps to wait for objects to stabilize in sim.""" num_trials_per_task: int = 50 """Number of rollouts per task.""" # --- Evaluation arguments --- video_out_path: str = "data/libero/videos" """Path to save videos.""" device: str = "cuda" """Device to use for evaluation.""" seed: int = 7 """Random Seed (for reproducibility)""" @draccus.wrap() def eval_libero(args: Args) -> None: # Set random seed torch.manual_seed(args.seed) np.random.seed(args.seed) # --- Load Policy --- policy = SmolVLAPolicy.from_pretrained(args.policy_path) policy.to(args.device) policy.eval() # --- Initialize LIBERO task suite --- benchmark_dict = benchmark.get_benchmark_dict() try: task_suite = benchmark_dict[args.task_suite_name]() except KeyError: raise ValueError( f"Unknown task suite: {args.task_suite_name}. " f"Available options are: {list(benchmark_dict.keys())}" ) num_tasks_in_suite = task_suite.n_tasks logging.info(f"Task suite: {args.task_suite_name}") pathlib.Path(args.video_out_path).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) if args.task_suite_name == "libero_spatial": max_steps = 220 # longest training demo has 193 steps elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_object": max_steps = 280 # longest training demo has 254 steps elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_goal": max_steps = 300 # longest training demo has 270 steps elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_10": max_steps = 520 # longest training demo has 505 steps elif args.task_suite_name == "libero_90": max_steps = 400 # longest training demo has 373 steps else: # Fallback for custom task suites max_steps = 520 # --- Evaluation Loop --- total_episodes, total_successes = 0, 0 for task_id in tqdm(range(num_tasks_in_suite), desc="Tasks"): # Get task task = task_suite.get_task(task_id) # Get default LIBERO initial states initial_states = task_suite.get_task_init_states(task_id) # Initialize LIBERO environment and task description env, task_description = _get_libero_env(task, LIBERO_ENV_RESOLUTION, args.seed) # Start episodes task_episodes, task_successes = 0, 0 for episode_idx in tqdm( range(min(args.num_trials_per_task, len(initial_states))), desc=f"Task {task_id}: {task.language}", leave=False, ): logging.info(f"\nTask: {task_description}") # Reset environment and policy env.reset() policy.reset() # Set initial states obs = env.set_init_state(initial_states[episode_idx]) # IMPORTANT: Do nothing for the first few timesteps because the simulator drops objects # and we need to wait for them to fall for _ in range(args.num_steps_wait): obs, _, _, _ = env.step(LIBERO_DUMMY_ACTION) # Setup t = 0 frames = [] done = False # Add initial frame agentview_image = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1]) # frames.append(agentview_image) # import ipdb; ipdb.set_trace() logging.info(f"Starting episode {task_episodes+1}...") while t < max_steps: try: # Get preprocessed image # IMPORTANT: rotate 180 degrees to match train preprocessing wrist_img = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["robot0_eye_in_hand_image"][::-1, ::-1]) agentview_image = np.ascontiguousarray(obs["agentview_image"][::-1, ::-1]) frames.append(agentview_image) # Prepare observations dict state = np.concatenate( ( obs["robot0_eef_pos"], _quat2axisangle(obs["robot0_eef_quat"]), obs["robot0_gripper_qpos"], ) ) observation = { "observation.images.image": torch.from_numpy(agentview_image / 255.0) .permute(2, 0, 1) .to(torch.float32) .to(args.device).unsqueeze(0), "observation.images.wrist_image": torch.from_numpy(wrist_img / 255.0) .permute(2, 0, 1) .to(torch.float32) .to(args.device).unsqueeze(0), "observation.state": torch.from_numpy(state).to(torch.float32).to(args.device).unsqueeze(0), "task": task_description, } # Query model to get action with torch.inference_mode(): action_tensor = policy.select_action(observation) action = action_tensor.cpu().numpy()[0] # action[-1] = 1 - action[-1] action = normalize_gripper_action(action, binarize=False) action = invert_gripper_action(action) # Execute action in environment obs, _, done, _ = env.step(action) if done: task_successes += 1 total_successes += 1 break t += 1 except Exception as e: logging.error(f"Caught exception: {e}") break task_episodes += 1 total_episodes += 1 # Save a replay video of the episode suffix = "success" if done else "failure" task_segment = task_description.replace(" ", "_").replace("/", "_") video_path = ( pathlib.Path(args.video_out_path) / f"rollout_task_{task_id}_episode_{episode_idx}_{task_segment}_{suffix}.mp4" ) fps = 30 writer = imageio.get_writer(video_path, fps=fps) for image in frames: writer.append_data(image) writer.close() logging.info(f"Saved video to {video_path}") # import ipdb; ipdb.set_trace() # Log current results logging.info(f"Success: {done}") if total_episodes > 0: logging.info(f"# episodes completed so far: {total_episodes}") logging.info(f"# successes: {total_successes} ({total_successes / total_episodes * 100:.1f}%)") # Log final results for the task if task_episodes > 0: logging.info(f"Task {task_id} success rate: {float(task_successes) / float(task_episodes):.2f}") if total_episodes > 0: logging.info(f"Cumulative success rate: {float(total_successes) / float(total_episodes):.2f}") logging.info("--- Evaluation finished ---") if total_episodes > 0: logging.info(f"Total success rate: {float(total_successes) / float(total_episodes):.2f}") logging.info(f"Total episodes: {total_episodes}") logging.info(f"Total successes: {total_successes}") # cv2.destroyAllWindows() def _get_libero_env(task, resolution, seed): """Initializes and returns the LIBERO environment, along with the task description.""" task_description = task.language task_bddl_file = pathlib.Path(get_libero_path("bddl_files")) / task.problem_folder / task.bddl_file env_args = { "bddl_file_name": str(task_bddl_file), "camera_heights": resolution, "camera_widths": resolution, } env = OffScreenRenderEnv(**env_args) env.seed(seed) # IMPORTANT: seed seems to affect object positions even when using fixed initial state return env, task_description def _quat2axisangle(quat): """ Copied from robosuite: https://github.com/ARISE-Initiative/robosuite/blob/eafb81f54ffc104f905ee48a16bb15f059176ad3/robosuite/utils/transform_utils.py#L490C1-L512C55 """ # clip quaternion if quat[3] > 1.0: quat[3] = 1.0 elif quat[3] < -1.0: quat[3] = -1.0 den = np.sqrt(1.0 - quat[3] * quat[3]) if math.isclose(den, 0.0): # This is (close to) a zero degree rotation, immediately return return np.zeros(3) return (quat[:3] * 2.0 * math.acos(quat[3])) / den if __name__ == "__main__": logging.basicConfig( level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s", handlers=[ logging.FileHandler("evaluation_log.txt"), logging.StreamHandler() # Optional: keeps logging in the terminal too ] ) eval_libero() ``` To run this script use: ```bash python lerobot/scripts/eval_LIBERO.py --policy_path=outputs/trainv5/libero_smolvla_scratch/checkpoints/067000/pretrained_model ``` If you run into this error: ```bash File "/home/tay/Documents/robo-intel-action/finetuning_lerobot/LIBERO/libero/libero/benchmark/__init__.py", line 164, in get_task_init_states init_states = torch.load(init_states_path) File "/home/tay/miniconda3/envs/lerobot/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 1524, in load raise pickle.UnpicklingError(_get_wo_message(str(e))) from None _pickle.UnpicklingError: Weights only load failed. This file can still be loaded, to do so you have two options, do those steps only if you trust the source of the checkpoint. ``` Change `libero.benchmark.__init__.py`, line 164 from: ```python init_states = torch.load(init_states_path) ``` to this: ``` init_states = torch.load(init_states_path, weights_only=False) ``` 4. Results The evaluation script outputs some rollouts and stats in terminal (I output them to `evaluation_log.txt`). ```txt 2025-08-07 10:49:34,622 - INFO - --- Evaluation finished --- 2025-08-07 10:49:34,622 - INFO - Total success rate: 0.71 2025-08-07 10:49:34,622 - INFO - Total episodes: 500 2025-08-07 10:49:34,622 - INFO - Total successes: 356 ``` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/606ee625-cd76-4260-a416-d45189540c22 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5028e74a-b558-4d0d-8b2b-d7d9aa63d1fb

I found that using accelerate for multi-gpu training with evaluation arguments causes this issue. Removing the following arguments in the training script resolved it for me:

--env.type=libero
--env.task=libero_10
--eval_freq=2000
--eval.batch_size=1
--eval.n_episodes=1


update: After switching to a different machine and using the latest repository code, I haven't encountered this problem again.

Hey @LeeZheXian!
As the error logs says:
```
ValueError: Feature mismatch between dataset/environment and policy config.
- Missing features: ['observation.images.top', 'observation.images.wrist']
- Extra features: ['observation.images.image', 'observation.images.image2']

Please ensure your dataset and policy use consistent feature names.
If your dataset uses different observation keys (e.g., cameras named differently), use the `--rename_map` argument, for example:
  --rename_map='{"observation.images.left": "observation.images.camera1", "observation.images.top": "observation.images.camera2"}'
```

You should pass a rename map during training, just add the following in the CI:
```
--rename_map='{
  "observation.images.image": "observation.images.top",
  "observation.images.image2": "observation.images.wrist"
}'
```
The reason we pass this, is to be able to remap between the camera (visual) keys the policy expects in your case ['observation.images.top', 'observation.images.wrist'] and what the environment provides: ['observation.images.image', 'observation.images.image2']

Hope this is clearer you !

comments.body:
Hello @RiccardoIzzo,

You should put the rename map also during evalaution, that's becasue your smolvla checkpoint take as input observation.images.image and observation.images.writst_image, whereas libero env gives to your policy image observation as observation.images.image and observation.images.image2.

So you can just pass:

```
--rename_map='{"observation.images.image":"observation.images.image","observation.images.image2":"observation.images.wrist_image"}'
```

Alternatively, you can edit the `config.json` of the policy and hard-code the names to `observation.images.image2`, instead of using the rename map dictionary every time.

It looks like you trained SmolVLA on your own dataset, which uses observation keys that differ from LIBERO, hence the mismatch.

Feel free to open the issue again, if the response didnt resolve it

title: Evaluation of Policies on Libero

body:
I'm opening this issue to report a discrepancy I've observed when evaluating fine-tuned π0 and π0.5 models on LIBERO benchmark.
The performance of them is lower than the success rates reported in the leaderboard and [original github repository](https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi).
- **Models:**
[lerobot/pi0_libero_finetuned](https://huggingface.co/lerobot/pi0_libero_finetuned)
[lerobot/pi05_libero_finetuned](https://huggingface.co/lerobot/pi05_libero_finetuned)

- **Observed success rates:**
pi0_libero_finetuned:
-- libero_spatial **69**%, libero_object **72**%, libero_goal **83**%, libero_10 **35**%, overall **64.75**%
pi05_libero_finetuned:
-- libero_spatial **77**%, libero_object **66**%, libero_goal **89**%, libero_10 **55**%, total **71.75**%

**Environment set up:**
Just clone latest LeRobot repository and install dependencies and run lerobot_eval.py

**Evaluation command:**
For π0:
`MUJOCO_GL="egl" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m lerobot.scripts.lerobot_eval --policy.path=lerobot/pi0_libero_finetuned --env.type=libero --env.task=libero_spatial,libero_object,libero_goal,libero_10 --eval.batch_size=1 --eval.n_episodes=10 --seed=3000`
For π0.5:
`MUJOCO_GL="egl" CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m lerobot.scripts.lerobot_eval --policy.path=lerobot/pi05_libero_finetuned --env.type=libero --env.task=libero_spatial,libero_object,libero_goal,libero_10 --eval.batch_size=1 --eval.n_episodes=10 --seed=3000 --policy.compile_model=false`


The reported success rates for both models are about 10-20% higher than the ovserved one.
I'm wondering if there are any known issues or specific configurations needed for these models that might not be documented.
Any insights or guidance on how to achieve the reported success rates would be greatly appreciated.

And I suggest to use seed 1000 as this is what we used to evaluate on

I used MuJoCo==**2.3.7** for evaluation. 

I upgraded MuJoCo to 3.3.2 and used seed=1000, and the success rates for π0 improved as follows
libero_spatial: 69% → **73**%
libero_object: 72% → **85**%
libero_goal: 83% → **80**%
libero_10: 35% → **46**%
overall: 64.75% → **71**%

These success rates are still lower than reported one.

```
# @package _global_

# Defaults for training for the PushT dataset as per https://github.com/real-stanford/diffusion_policy.
# Note: We do not track EMA model weights as we discovered it does not improve the results. See
#       https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/134 for more details.

seed: 100000
dataset_repo_id: lerobot/aloha_sim_transfer_cube_scripted
root: /data/dataset/HuggingFace-Download-Accelerator/hf_hub
 
override_dataset_stats:
  # TODO(rcadene, alexander-soare): should we remove image stats as well? do we use a pretrained vision model?
  observation.images.top:
    mean: [[[0.485]], [[0.456]], [[0.406]]]  # (c,1,1)
    std: [[[0.229]], [[0.224]], [[0.225]]]  # (c,1,1)
  # TODO(rcadene, alexander-soare): we override state and action stats to use the same as the pretrained model
  # from the original codebase, but we should remove these and train our own pretrained model
  # observation.state:
  #   min: [13.456424, 32.938293]
  #   max: [496.14618, 510.9579]
  # action:
  #   min: [12.0, 25.0]
  #   max: [511.0, 511.0]

training:
  offline_steps: 200000
  online_steps: 0
  eval_freq: 20000
  save_freq: 20000
  save_checkpoint: true

  batch_size: 20
  grad_clip_norm: 10
  lr: 1.0e-4
  lr_scheduler: cosine
  lr_warmup_steps: 500
  adam_betas: [0.95, 0.999]
  adam_eps: 1.0e-8
  adam_weight_decay: 1.0e-6
  online_steps_between_rollouts: 1

  delta_timestamps:
    observation.images.top: "[i / ${fps} for i in range(1 - ${policy.n_obs_steps}, 1)]"
    observation.state: "[i / ${fps} for i in range(1 - ${policy.n_obs_steps}, 1)]"
    action: "[i / ${fps} for i in range(1 - ${policy.n_obs_steps}, 1 - ${policy.n_obs_steps} + ${policy.horizon})]"

  # The original implementation doesn't sample frames for the last 7 steps,
  # which avoids excessive padding and leads to improved training results.
  drop_n_last_frames: 7  # ${policy.horizon} - ${policy.n_action_steps} - ${policy.n_obs_steps} + 1

eval:
  n_episodes: 25
  batch_size: 25

policy:
  name: diffusion

  # Input / output structure.
  n_obs_steps: 2
  horizon: 16
  n_action_steps: 8

  input_shapes:
    # TODO(rcadene, alexander-soare): add variables for height and width from the dataset/env?
    observation.images.top: [3, 480, 640]
    observation.state: ["${env.state_dim}"]
  output_shapes:
    action: ["${env.action_dim}"]

  # Normalization / Unnormalization
  input_normalization_modes:
    observation.images.top: mean_std 
    observation.state: min_max
  output_normalization_modes:
    action: min_max

  # Architecture / modeling.
  # Vision backbone.
  vision_backbone: resnet18
  crop_shape: [440, 560]
  crop_is_random: False
  pretrained_backbone_weights: null
  use_group_norm: True
  spatial_softmax_num_keypoints: 32
  # Unet.
  down_dims: [512, 1024, 2048]
  kernel_size: 5
  n_groups: 8
  diffusion_step_embed_dim: 128 
  use_film_scale_modulation: True
  # Noise scheduler.
  noise_scheduler_type: DDPM
  num_train_timesteps: 100
  beta_schedule: squaredcos_cap_v2
  beta_start: 0.0001
  beta_end: 0.02
  prediction_type: epsilon # epsilon / sample
  clip_sample: True
  clip_sample_range: 1.0
 
  # Inference
  num_inference_steps: null  # if not provided, defaults to `num_train_timesteps`

  # Loss computation
  do_mask_loss_for_padding: false
  use_l1_loss: False
```

body:
Hi all,

edit: i wondered how the setup can be amended since the debugging resources are scarce. I am working on π0 with lerobot as embodiment for research publication. Is it recommended to use the open-sourced π0 from openpi instead of the lerobot versionof π0? 

I am training the pi0 base model (under the lerobot repo) with hf dataset aloha_sim_transfer_cube_human and lerobot/aloha_sim_insertion_human, for 100k steps. For all of the eval results, the arm's got jerky movements and is not able to pick up any objects. I have checked and tried debugging every parameters for the setup to work. Here is my command for training: 

```bash
TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false" python -m lerobot.scripts.train \
    --dataset.root=/dataset/lerobot/aloha_sim_transfer_cube_human \
    --dataset.repo_id=lerobot/aloha_sim_transfer_cube_human \
    --env.type=aloha \
    --env.task=AlohaInsertion-v0 \
    --policy.type=pi0 \
    --policy.n_obs_steps=1 \ 
    --policy.chunk_size=10 \
    --policy.n_action_steps=10 \
    --policy.max_state_dim=32 \
    --policy.max_action_dim=32 \
    --policy.resize_imgs_with_padding='[224, 224]' \
    --policy.empty_cameras=2 \
    --policy.adapt_to_pi_aloha=true \      
    --policy.use_delta_joint_actions_aloha=false \
    --policy.tokenizer_max_length=48 \
    --policy.proj_width=1024 \
    --policy.num_steps=10 \
    --policy.use_cache=true \
    --policy.attention_implementation=eager \
    --policy.freeze_vision_encoder=true \ 
    --policy.train_expert_only=false \ 
    --policy.train_state_proj=true \
    --policy.optimizer_lr=2.5e-05 \
    --policy.optimizer_betas='[0.9, 0.95]' \
```

```python
def normalize_gripper_action(action, binarize=True):
    """
    Changes gripper action (last dimension of action vector) from [0,1] to [-1,+1].
    Necessary for some environments (not Bridge) because the dataset wrapper standardizes gripper actions to [0,1].
    Note that unlike the other action dimensions, the gripper action is not normalized to [-1,+1] by default by
    the dataset wrapper.

    Normalization formula: y = 2 * (x - orig_low) / (orig_high - orig_low) - 1
    """
    # Just normalize the last action to [-1,+1].
    orig_low, orig_high = 0.0, 1.0
    action[..., -1] = 2 * (action[..., -1] - orig_low) / (orig_high - orig_low) - 1

    if binarize:
        # Binarize to -1 or +1.
        action[..., -1] = np.sign(action[..., -1])

    return action

def invert_gripper_action(action):
    """
    Flips the sign of the gripper action (last dimension of action vector).
    This is necessary for some environments where -1 = open, +1 = close, since
    the RLDS dataloader aligns gripper actions such that 0 = close, 1 = open.
    """
    action[..., -1] = action[..., -1] * -1.0
```

### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- LeRobot: commit at 14a15f90
- Robot: SO-101
- Policy: SmolVLA
- OS: macOS

- the output of `lerobot-info`

- LeRobot version: 0.4.4
- Platform: macOS-15.7.2-arm64-arm-64bit
- Python version: 3.11.9
- Huggingface Hub version: 0.35.3
- Datasets version: 4.1.1
- Numpy version: 2.2.6
- FFmpeg version: 7.1.1
- PyTorch version: 2.7.1
- Is PyTorch built with CUDA support?: False
- Cuda version: N/A
- GPU model: N/A
- Using GPU in script?: <fill in>
- lerobot scripts: ['lerobot-calibrate', 'lerobot-dataset-viz', 'lerobot-edit-dataset', 'lerobot-eval', 'lerobot-find-cameras', 'lerobot-find-joint-limits', 'lerobot-find-port', 'lerobot-imgtransform-viz', 'lerobot-info', 'lerobot-record', 'lerobot-replay', 'lerobot-setup-can', 'lerobot-setup-motors', 'lerobot-teleoperate', 'lerobot-train', 'lerobot-train-tokenizer']
```

### Description

We observe a noticeable difference in task success between Sync (local) inference and Async inference.

In our setup, policies trained with the current version of LeRobot perform reliably under Sync inference, but often fail under Async inference. In contrast, policies trained with older LeRobot versions and then migrated to the current format tend to show much smaller degradation when run with Async inference.

The issue is reproducible across multiple runs of the same task and does not appear to be limited to a single dataset or model checkpoint.

### Context & Reproduction


#### Observed behavior

* Sync inference achieves relatively stable task success.
* Async inference shows significantly lower success rates.
* The robot arm usually moves close to the target, but precise actions (e.g. grasping) often fail under Async inference.

A consistent difference we observed is how the policy was trained:

* Policies trained with older LeRobot versions (around commit 483be9a ) tend to retain reasonable performance under Async inference.
* Policies fine-tuned from the same base model using the current version of LeRobot often show severe degradation under Async inference, even when trained on the same dataset migrated to Dataset v3.


#### Policies and datasets used

| Policy         | Training setup                               | Dataset version   | Link                                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Old (migrated) | Fine-tuned with older LeRobot, then migrated | Dataset v2.1      | [https://huggingface.co/yutaro-kimura-acs/so101_pp_blue_box_policy_01_migrated](https://huggingface.co/yutaro-kimura-acs/so101_pp_blue_box_policy_01_migrated)             |
| New            | Fine-tuned with current LeRobot              | Dataset v2.1 → v3 (Migrated with [conversion script](https://huggingface.co/docs/lerobot/lerobot-dataset-v3#migrate-v21--v30)) | [https://huggingface.co/aShunSasaki/so101_pp_blue_box_yk_dataset_policy_v30_cp_20000](https://huggingface.co/aShunSasaki/so101_pp_blue_box_yk_dataset_policy_v30_cp_20000) |

Both policies were fine-tuned from the same base model (`smolvla_base`) using the same dataset:
[https://huggingface.co/datasets/yutaro-kimura-acs/so101_pp_blue_box](https://huggingface.co/datasets/yutaro-kimura-acs/so101_pp_blue_box)


#### Videos

* Old (migrated):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d362ed09-112c-46ec-adec-7058c4b6ea3f


* New:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3c6fcd8-f169-4324-8aba-9148af304e41

#### Task success rates

| Policy         | Sync inference | Async inference | Notes                                    |
| -------------- | :------------: | :-------------: | ---------------------------------------- |
| Old (migrated) |     80–90%     |       **~50%**      | `input_features` shape: `[3, 720, 1280]` |
| New (current)  |     80–90%     |        **0%**       | `input_features` shape: `[3, 256, 256]`  |

* Robot: SO-101
* Task: Pick-and-place (blue box)
* Policy architecture: SmolVLA (`smolvla_base` fine-tuned)


#### Possible contributing factor

One possible factor we identified is a difference in image preprocessing between Sync and Async inference paths.

In the async path, the camera image appears to be resized to match `policy.config.input_features` before being passed to the model. For policies where `input_features` reflects the dataset storage resolution (e.g. 256×256), this results in the camera image being resized from its native resolution (1280×720) to a square shape.

In contrast, Sync inference does not resize the image at this stage and relies on the model’s internal `resize_with_pad`, which preserves aspect ratio.

This behavior seems related to the image resizing discrepancy discussed in #2475, and may help explain why older migrated policies behave more robustly under Async inference.


#### Configuration differences observed

While investigating this issue, we also compared the policy configuration files between older migrated policies and newly fine-tuned ones.

One notable difference is the `input_features` image shape:

* Older migrated policies use the camera’s native resolution (e.g. `[3, 720, 1280]`)
* Newly fine-tuned policies use the dataset storage resolution (e.g. `[3, 256, 256]`)

This difference appears to affect how images are handled in the async inference path, where the input image is resized to match `input_features` before being passed to the policy.

We are not fully sure whether this alone explains the observed behavior, but it stood out during the comparison.

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell
No explicit runtime errors or stack traces were observed.
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

This issue may be related to the image preprocessing difference discussed in:

- https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/issues/2475

That issue focuses on image resizing behavior specifically, while this ticket aims to describe the broader performance gap observed between Sync and Async inference, as well as the difference between older migrated models and newly trained ones.

At the moment, using a policy trained with an older LeRobot version and migrating it to the current format appears to mitigate the issue.

comments.author: aShunSasaki
comments.body:
@mgm136044 

At the moment, there isn’t a supported way to downgrade a dataset from v3.0 back to v2.1.

What I did instead was:
1. Use an older version of LeRobot to collect a v2.1 dataset, and train the policy in the same environment.
2. Then switch to the current version of LeRobot and run the following to migrate the trained policy:

```
python -m lerobot.processor.migrate_policy_normalization \
  --pretrained-path your-username/your-old-policy \
  --push-to-hub
```

So the dataset collection and training are done with the old version, and only the policy migration is done with the current version.

comments.author: rylinjames
comments.body: the sync-vs-async gap on smolvla + so-101 is almost always one of two things: (1) action-chunk horizon mismatch (sync replays the full chunk, async often only uses the first k actions then requests a new one, so drift accumulates on precise grasps), or (2) observation timestamp alignment (async server processes a slightly stale obs, old-version checkpoints were trained with more temporal smoothing so they tolerate it). can you check the `n_action_steps` / chunk-consumption setting on the async client vs the sync path? that's the first thing to pin. reflex won't fix the training-time root cause here, but we do provide a deterministic onnx+fp16-trt deploy for smolvla with cos=+1.0 parity, useful for isolating whether async drift is in the server/scheduler or the policy itself. github.com/rylinjames/reflex-vla has good-first-issues tagged, or dm romirj on discord / playindus@gmail.com for collaborator access.

### Description

**Issue Description:**

I have successfully installed LeRobot 0.4.2 on my Jetson Orin using PyTorch 2.5.0 + torchvision 0.20.0 (the latest versions officially supported on JetPack 6.x). The entire pipeline runs without crashes.

The problem: The model outputs incorrect actions during inference on the real robot. The same SmolVLA model, running with the same scene setup and identical configuration on an x86_64 laptop, successfully completes the task.
**Key observation:**

-     On the Jetson, torchcodec is not available (cannot be installed on ARM64 + JetPack due to glibc / binary compatibility issues). LeRobot automatically falls back to pyav for video decoding.
-     On the x86_64 laptop, torchcodec is installed and used as the video decoding backend.

What works: No runtime errors, model loads successfully, inference loop runs.
What doesn't work: The robot executes seemingly random/unexpected movements instead of the intended task.
**My questions:**

1.Could the difference in video decoding backend (pyav vs torchcodec) be the root cause? 
2.Is torchvision ≥ 0.21 strictly required for correct SmolVLA inference, or is the real requirement that torchcodec must be available? The version constraint might be a proxy for ensuring the right decoding backend.
3.Are there any known differences in tensor output between pyav and torchcodec when decoding the same video frame? For example, differences in:
      (1) Color channel order (RGB vs BGR)
      (2) Pixel value range (0-255 vs 0-1, or different normalization)
      (3) Frame cropping/resizing behavior
      (4)Precision (uint8 vs float32)
4.Is there any recommended way to force torchcodec on Jetson ARM64? Or alternatively, is there a way to make pyav produce bit-identical tensors to torchcodec so that model outputs remain consistent?

**Additional context:**

-       The x86_64 environment uses conda; Jetson uses venv (same Python version 3.10 for both)
-       Both environments use the same model file downloaded from Hugging Face Hub
-       Inference script is identical
-       Physical scene setup (camera positions, object placement) is identical between tests
-       The issue is about inference correctness, not runtime errors or speed

Any insights would be greatly appreciated!

@milong26 have you found a way to correct the URDF "zero" joint values with your personal calibration?

The FK uses the URDF joint origins as the reference. Your personal calibration ensures that when your robot is at its physical "middle/zero" position, the motors report values around mid = (range_min + range_max) / 2.                                                                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
BUT: If your physical "middle" position during calibration doesn't exactly match the URDF's expected zero pose, the FK will have an offset.                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                                          
The so101_new_calib.urdf was designed with joint origins that match a "standard" calibration procedure. If your calibration procedure differed slightly (e.g., robot wasn't perfectly at the expected pose when you pressed "Enter"), there will be discrepancies.

```Dockerfile
FROM huggingface/lerobot-gpu:latest
```

Hello, everyone

Could you please explain why in `LiberoEnv.reset()` method, the environment is reset after setting the initial state [(code)](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/f6b16f6d97155e3ce34ab2a1ec145e9413588197/src/lerobot/envs/libero.py#L242)? body:
### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
lerobot==0.4.3
```

### Description

## Problem Description

When running evaluation with `lerobot-eval`, we observed an issue where the evaluation environment diversity is unintentionally limited by the value of:

```bash
--eval.batch_size = n
```

Specifically, during evaluation, **the number of unique environment initial states is effectively capped at `n`**, rather than increasing across evaluation batches. As a result:

* Only `n` initial states are ever evaluated
* Subsequent evaluation batches reuse the same initial environments
* Evaluation diversity and robustness are significantly underestimated

This issue is based on **LIBERO environments**.

---

## Related Pull Requests

This behavior appears closely related to previous evaluation and synchronization fixes discussed in:

* [https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/2419](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/2419)
* [https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/2817](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/pull/2817)

While these PRs address important issues around evaluation determinism and environment synchronization, **`lerobot-eval` still lacks explicit control over environment initial state IDs**, which leads to the diversity limitation described above.

---

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `lerobot-eval` with a policy and set:

   ```bash
   --eval.batch_size = n
   ```
2. Observe or log the environment initial state identifier (e.g. `init_state_id`)
3. Notice that across all evaluation batches, only the first `n` initial states are used repeatedly

---

## Proposed Fix

### 1️⃣ Add explicit `init_state_id` control to `LiberoEnv`

In `lerobot.envs.libero.LiberoEnv`, add:

```python
def set_init_state_id(self, init_state_id):
    self._init_state_id = init_state_id
```

This allows external control of the environment initialization during evaluation.

---

### 2️⃣ Synchronize `init_state_id` across `SyncVectorEnv`

In `lerobot_eval.py`, introduce a helper function:

```python
def set_sync_env_init_state_id(
    vec_env: gym.vector.SyncVectorEnv,
    init_state_ids: list,
):
    """
    Set init_state_id for all envs in a SyncVectorEnv.

    Args:
        vec_env: gym.vector.SyncVectorEnv
        init_state_ids: sequence[int]
    """
    for idx, env in enumerate(vec_env.envs):
        cur_id = init_state_ids[idx]

        # unwrap common gym wrappers
        if hasattr(env, "set_init_state_id"):
            env.set_init_state_id(cur_id)
```

---

### 3️⃣ Advance `init_state_id` per evaluation batch

Inside the evaluation loop (e.g. `eval_policy`), compute unique initialization IDs per batch:

```python
init_state_ids = [
    i
    for i in range(
        batch_ix * env.num_envs,
        (batch_ix + 1) * env.num_envs
    )
]
```

Call `set_sync_env_init_state_id(env, init_state_ids)` **before** `env.reset()`.

### Context & Reproduction

_No response_

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell

```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [x] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

### Additional Info / Workarounds

_No response_

Hi I used Moss robot to play with and train ACT policy, when it comes to one lego piece, it can finish grabbing task at high success rate after recording 50+ episodes with different pose & location variants, but generalization on multi-piece random location is not promising.

When I started to add complexity (for example 6 pieces with different colors like the picture below), and place the lego pieces a little bit randomly, record one episode continuously until all the pieces are grabbed (other than 1 piece 1 episode). furthermore,  were recorded with order
![IMG_4681 HEIC](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbe58ebc-0690-4563-ab1d-cf0660305611)

Here is what I found:
1. The trained policy can not work if the gripping sequence is randomized, in other words it has to keep a fixed spacial order e.g. from upper left to down right.
2. The trained policy can not work if the [location, color, pose] combination was not seen in training dataset, especially location combos 
3. At first I suspected only iPhone and Mac fixed cameras can not give enough depth perception, so I bought a wide-angle USB camera mounted it on the gripper, as a result success rate didn't get higher. 
![20241204141608](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/346a6c22-7516-4854-ac1f-5d7029af5336)

4. Enlarging dataset size to 120+ episodes didn't give obvious change.




I was wondering how to improve this task, is the method I used to record data wrong or due to the generalization of ACT is limited?  

Looking forward to hearing answers or experience

@astroyat My original thought is that reseting to the start position would be time consuming, so I haven't tried this method, do you have experience about this, in your experiment did 1 piece 1 episode help improve success rate?

 I think the essential problem is whether this algorithm can learn planning in a long-time picking scenario

Here is my recording with one camera, starting from top position instead of rest position and the tip is modded to be wider. https://huggingface.co/spaces/lerobot/visualize_dataset?dataset=astroyat%2Fcube&episode=0 Here is my eval with high success rate, the eval graph matches the recording graph. https://huggingface.co/spaces/lerobot/visualize_dataset?dataset=astroyat%2Feval_cube&episode=0 I tried pick all 5 legos in one episode and the joint graph is chaotic, so, the eval was very bad. But disappointingly, the behavior is similar to the previous one, when the lego grasping order is learned in dataset it performs good, but when the state is hard to define order, ACT starts to collapse. let me give an example, I was recording data in this order, left-right and up-down, and followed a dummy block rule (subjectively determined) indicated by the black dotted line, the number is the order I grasp legos. The upper block prioritized over below ones, and within block, left pieces prioritized over right ones. When the lego piece is at the junction of the blocks, robot arm will stuck somewhere in the middle (e.g. in the middle of the blue and the green like below). if not intervening by relocating the state to somewhere model has seen, it will never get autocorrect. I think one reason is even humans cannot maintain consistent and coherent actions in those situations. Does this mean the sequence of unordered grasping is very difficult to learn in the current algorithm framework? Any idea or comment?

This matters because pretraining data often contains non-mirrored real Franka observations, while LIBERO finetuning currently uses mirrored observations. Aligning the image modality would likely improve evaluation quality and reduce unnecessary visual domain mismatch. A possible fix could be to make a change in the LIBERO wrapper to horizontally flip camera observations back to the real-world Franka orientation, and then provide h-flipped versions of LIBERO datasets (e.g., lerobot/libero). Happy to pull request if the LeRobot team wants this fix. ### Context & Reproduction _No response_ ### Relevant logs or stack trace ```Shell ``` ### Checklist - [ ] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate. - [ ] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch. - [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem. ### Additional Info / Workarounds _No response_

@jadechoghari  hi, the checkpoint https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceVLA/smolvla_libero use `expert_width_multiplier=0.5`, and all 32 layers of smolvlm2, while in the paper it should use  `expert_width_multiplier=0.75` and 16 layers.

BTW this checkpoint is unexpectedly large (1.22GB than 907mb), might caused by using all 32 layers of vlm2.

I also found a checkpoint https://huggingface.co/lerobot/smolvla_libero/tree/main released by [pepijn223](https://huggingface.co/pepijn223)(4th author of the paper), but it's even worse:
It claims in `config.cfg` that it requies 3 cameras(libero has 2 only), and observation state of 6 (should be 7, both claws have one state) .
Its config use `expert_width_multiplier=0.75`, but actually lerobot will refuse to load it, because of mis-matching dim size(expect 720 got 480), impling that the checkpoint is actually using `expert_width_multiplier=0.5` .

That's quite confusing, could you please clearify what these checkpoints are actually for?
