body:
Hi, 

Thanks for sharing this brilliant package for real-2-sim evaluation!

I'm trying to run SimplerEnv inside a docker on a linux server with GPU support. The environment can be successfully created and reset, but a `Segmentation fault (core dumped)` error shows up when calling `env.step()`. I have followed the troubleshooting instructions in README, but still can't solve this issue. Could you please help have a look at what may be the issues here? Thanks a lot for your help!

Below is the docker file I use (modified from ManiSkill's [dockerfile](https://github.com/haosulab/ManiSkill/blob/main/docker/Dockerfile)) 
```
# Base Image
FROM nvidia/cudagl:11.3.1-devel-ubuntu20.04

# Args need to be below FROM!
ARG USER_ID
ARG PYTHON_VERSION=3.10

ENV NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES all

# Install os-level packages
RUN apt-get update && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    bash-completion \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    curl \
    git \
    htop \
    libegl1 \
    libxext6 \
    libjpeg-dev \
    libpng-dev  \
    libvulkan1 \
    rsync \
    tmux \
    unzip \
    vim \
    vulkan-utils \
    wget \
    xvfb \
    # lib for SAPIEN rendering
    libglvnd-dev \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install (mini) conda
RUN curl -o ~/miniconda.sh https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh && \
    chmod +x ~/miniconda.sh && \
    ~/miniconda.sh -b -p /opt/conda && \
    rm ~/miniconda.sh && \
    /opt/conda/bin/conda init && \
    /opt/conda/bin/conda install -y python="$PYTHON_VERSION" && \
    /opt/conda/bin/conda clean -ya

ENV PATH /opt/conda/bin:$PATH
SHELL ["/bin/bash", "-c"]

# https://github.com/haosulab/ManiSkill/issues/9
COPY docker/nvidia_icd.json /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/nvidia_icd.json
COPY docker/nvidia_layers.json /etc/vulkan/implicit_layer.d/nvidia_layers.json

# env
RUN git clone https://github.com/simpler-env/SimplerEnv --recurse-submodules
RUN pip install -e ./SimplerEnv/ManiSkill2_real2sim
RUN pip install -e ./SimplerEnv

# Change permissions
RUN useradd --shell /bin/bash -u ${USER_ID} -o -d /user user

# Set python ENV variables
ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
```
The docker installation seems to work fine. And I'm using the same test script as given in [README](https://github.com/simpler-env/SimplerEnv?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started).

I've been running my policy in the SimPLER environment (WidowX tasks), and the success metric feels really off.

The environment often reports success way too early

- e.g., the object is near the target but not actually placed correctly
- sometimes the robot hasn’t even finished the action (like releasing the object)

There are cases where the task is clearly about to fail (e.g., object could fall before completion), but it still gets counted as success
In some cases, the outcome is just plain wrong, but still marked as success

- object not in the right place
- visibly incorrect behavior

The following videos were marked as success.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25e35821-ac0f-4464-bdbc-253327841c9e

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ceb55197-4551-4070-a096-e1f5b8815c58

The reported success rate looks much higher than it actually is. It makes it hard to properly evaluate and compare policies. It also becomes an issue if you're training policies using this environment, since the reward/signal is misleading.

It would really help if the success conditions were stricter, for example:

- ensuring the object is actually placed correctly (not just nearby)
- checking stability (not about to fall)
- avoiding triggering success before the action is complete

comments.author: xuanlinli17
comments.body:
I checked with the authors and I don't think there is action ensembling or action history. Here is the updated code, which you can try:

```
from typing import Optional, Sequence
import os
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from transforms3d.euler import euler2axangle
from transformers import AutoModelForVision2Seq, AutoProcessor
from PIL import Image
import torch
import cv2 as cv


class OpenVLAInference:
    def __init__(
        self,
        saved_model_path: str = "openvla/openvla-7b",
        unnorm_key: Optional[str] = None,
        policy_setup: str = "widowx_bridge",
        horizon: int = 1,
        pred_action_horizon: int = 1,
        exec_horizon: int = 1,
        image_size: list[int] = [224, 224],
        action_scale: float = 1.0,
    ) -> None:
        os.environ["TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM"] = "false"
        if policy_setup == "widowx_bridge":
            unnorm_key = "bridge_orig" if unnorm_key is None else unnorm_key
            self.sticky_gripper_num_repeat = 1
        elif policy_setup == "google_robot":
            unnorm_key = "fractal20220817_data" if unnorm_key is None else unnorm_key
            self.sticky_gripper_num_repeat = 15
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"Policy setup {policy_setup} not supported for octo models. The other datasets can be found in the huggingface config.json file."
            )
        self.policy_setup = policy_setup
        self.unnorm_key = unnorm_key

        print(f"*** policy_setup: {policy_setup}, unnorm_key: {unnorm_key} ***")
        self.processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(saved_model_path, trust_remote_code=True)
        self.vla = AutoModelForVision2Seq.from_pretrained(
            "openvla/openvla-7b",
            attn_implementation="flash_attention_2",  # [Optional] Requires `flash_attn`
            torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
            low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
            trust_remote_code=True,
        ).cuda()

        self.image_size = image_size
        self.action_scale = action_scale
        self.horizon = horizon
        self.pred_action_horizon = pred_action_horizon
        self.exec_horizon = exec_horizon

        self.sticky_action_is_on = False
        self.gripper_action_repeat = 0
        self.sticky_gripper_action = 0.0
        self.previous_gripper_action = None

        self.task = None
        self.task_description = None
        self.num_image_history = 0

    def reset(self, task_description: str) -> None:
        self.task_description = task_description
        self.num_image_history = 0

        self.sticky_action_is_on = False
        self.gripper_action_repeat = 0
        self.sticky_gripper_action = 0.0
        self.previous_gripper_action = None

    def step(
        self, image: np.ndarray, task_description: Optional[str] = None, *args, **kwargs
    ) -> tuple[dict[str, np.ndarray], dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
        """
        Input:
            image: np.ndarray of shape (H, W, 3), uint8
            task_description: Optional[str], task description; if different from previous task description, policy state is reset
        Output:
            raw_action: dict; raw policy action output
            action: dict; processed action to be sent to the maniskill2 environment, with the following keys:
                - 'world_vector': np.ndarray of shape (3,), xyz translation of robot end-effector
                - 'rot_axangle': np.ndarray of shape (3,), axis-angle representation of end-effector rotation
                - 'gripper': np.ndarray of shape (1,), gripper action
                - 'terminate_episode': np.ndarray of shape (1,), 1 if episode should be terminated, 0 otherwise
        """
        if task_description is not None:
            if task_description != self.task_description:
                self.reset(task_description)

        assert image.dtype == np.uint8
        image = self._resize_image(image)

        image: Image.Image = Image.fromarray(image)
        prompt = task_description

        # predict action (7-dof; un-normalize for bridgev2)
        inputs = self.processor(prompt, image).to("cuda:0", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
        raw_actions = self.vla.predict_action(**inputs, unnorm_key=self.unnorm_key, do_sample=False)[None]
        # print(f"*** raw actions {raw_actions} ***")

        raw_action = {
            "world_vector": np.array(raw_actions[0, :3]),
            "rotation_delta": np.array(raw_actions[0, 3:6]),
            "open_gripper": np.array(raw_actions[0, 6:7]),  # range [0, 1]; 1 = open; 0 = close
        }

        # process raw_action to obtain the action to be sent to the maniskill2 environment
        action = {}
        action["world_vector"] = raw_action["world_vector"] * self.action_scale
        action_rotation_delta = np.asarray(raw_action["rotation_delta"], dtype=np.float64)
        roll, pitch, yaw = action_rotation_delta
        action_rotation_ax, action_rotation_angle = euler2axangle(roll, pitch, yaw)
        action_rotation_axangle = action_rotation_ax * action_rotation_angle
        action["rot_axangle"] = action_rotation_axangle * self.action_scale

        if self.policy_setup == "google_robot":
            current_gripper_action = raw_action["open_gripper"]
            if self.previous_gripper_action is None:
                relative_gripper_action = np.array([0])
            else:
                relative_gripper_action = self.previous_gripper_action - current_gripper_action
            self.previous_gripper_action = current_gripper_action

            if np.abs(relative_gripper_action) > 0.5 and (not self.sticky_action_is_on):
                self.sticky_action_is_on = True
                self.sticky_gripper_action = relative_gripper_action

            if self.sticky_action_is_on:
                self.gripper_action_repeat += 1
                relative_gripper_action = self.sticky_gripper_action

            if self.gripper_action_repeat == self.sticky_gripper_num_repeat:
                self.sticky_action_is_on = False
                self.gripper_action_repeat = 0
                self.sticky_gripper_action = 0.0

            action["gripper"] = relative_gripper_action

        elif self.policy_setup == "widowx_bridge":
            action["gripper"] = 2.0 * (raw_action["open_gripper"] > 0.5) - 1.0

        action["terminate_episode"] = np.array([0.0])

        return raw_action, action

    def _resize_image(self, image: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        image = cv.resize(image, tuple(self.image_size), interpolation=cv.INTER_AREA)
        return image

    def visualize_epoch(
        self, predicted_raw_actions: Sequence[np.ndarray], images: Sequence[np.ndarray], save_path: str
    ) -> None:
        images = [self._resize_image(image) for image in images]
        ACTION_DIM_LABELS = ["x", "y", "z", "roll", "pitch", "yaw", "grasp"]

        img_strip = np.concatenate(np.array(images[::3]), axis=1)

        # set up plt figure
        figure_layout = [["image"] * len(ACTION_DIM_LABELS), ACTION_DIM_LABELS]
        plt.rcParams.update({"font.size": 12})
        fig, axs = plt.subplot_mosaic(figure_layout)
        fig.set_size_inches([45, 10])

        # plot actions
        pred_actions = np.array(
            [
                np.concatenate([a["world_vector"], a["rotation_delta"], a["open_gripper"]], axis=-1)
                for a in predicted_raw_actions
            ]
        )
        for action_dim, action_label in enumerate(ACTION_DIM_LABELS):
            # actions have batch, horizon, dim, in this example we just take the first action for simplicity
            axs[action_label].plot(pred_actions[:, action_dim], label="predicted action")
            axs[action_label].set_title(action_label)
            axs[action_label].set_xlabel("Time in one episode")

        axs["image"].imshow(img_strip)
        axs["image"].set_xlabel("Time in one episode (subsampled)")
        plt.legend()
        plt.savefig(save_path)
```

Just follow treating processes of OpenVLA 
```
def libero_dataset_transform(trajectory: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    # gripper action is in -1 (open)...1 (close) --> clip to 0...1, flip --> +1 = open, 0 = close
    gripper_action = trajectory["action"][:, -1:]
    gripper_action = invert_gripper_actions(tf.clip_by_value(gripper_action, 0, 1))
    
    trajectory["action"] = tf.concat(
        [
            trajectory["action"][:, :6],
            gripper_action,
        ],
        axis=1,
    )
    # trajectory["observation"]["EEF_state"] = trajectory["observation"]["state"][:, :6]
    # trajectory["observation"]["gripper_state"] = trajectory["observation"]["state"][:, -2:]  # 2D gripper state
    
    trajectory["observation"]["proprio"] = tf.concat(
        (
            trajectory["observation"]["state"][:, :6],
            trajectory["observation"]["state"][:, -2:],
        ),
        axis=-1,
    )
    return trajectory
```

I only used the evaluation script `run_libero_eval_octo.py` provided in the official OpenVLA library, but I implemented functions related to Octo in `openvla_util.py`, for example:

```
def get_octo(cfg):
    """Loads and returns an Octo model from checkpoint."""
    octo = OctoModel.load_pretrained(cfg.pretrained_checkpoint)
    return octo


def get_octo_action(octo, obs, task_label, unnorm_key, center_crop=False):
    """Generates an action with the Octo policy (currently only supports one-step inference).
    
    Args:
        octo: OctoModel instance
        obs: observation dict containing 'full_image'
        task_label: string describing the task
        unnorm_key: key for unnormalization statistics
        center_crop: whether to apply center crop augmentation
    """
    # Convert observation to the format expected by Octo
    img = obs["full_image"]
    if center_crop:
        batch_size = 1
        crop_scale = 0.9

        # Convert to TF Tensor and record original data type (should be tf.uint8)
        img = tf.convert_to_tensor(img)
        orig_dtype = img.dtype

        # Convert to data type tf.float32 and values between [0,1]
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, tf.float32)

        # Crop and then resize back to original size
        img = crop_and_resize(img, crop_scale, batch_size)

        # Convert back to original data type
        img = tf.clip_by_value(img, 0, 1)
        img = tf.image.convert_image_dtype(img, orig_dtype, saturate=True)

        # Convert back to numpy array
        img = img.numpy()

    observations = {
        "image_primary": np.array(img)[None, None],  # Add batch and history dimensions
        "timestep_pad_mask": np.array([[True]]),  # No padding
        "proprio": np.array(obs['state'])[None, None]  # Reshape proprio to have batch and history dimensions
    }
    
    # Create task specification
    task = octo.create_tasks(texts=[task_label])
    
    # Get action from model
    action = octo.sample_actions(
        observations=observations,
        tasks=task,
        unnormalization_statistics=octo.dataset_statistics["action"],
        rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(0)  # Fixed seed for deterministic behavior
    )
    
    # Remove batch dimension and return
    return action[0][0]
```

title: The details of fine-tuning Octo using LIBERO

body:
## Problem Description

I am reproducing results using the official script and model for the LIBERO-Object benchmark. However, I consistently observe a much lower success rate compared to the numbers reported in the original paper.

**Success Rate Comparison:**

| Benchmark      | My Success Rate | Paper Reported |
| -------------- | --------------- | -------------- |
| LIBERO-Spatial | 85%             | 84.7% ± 0.9%   |
| LIBERO-Object  | 68%🤔      | 88.4% ± 0.8%   |
| LIBERO-Goal    | 75.8%           | 79.2% ± 1.0%   |
| LIBERO-Long    | 55.8%           | 53.7% ± 1.3%   |

The issue is especially significant for **LIBERO-Object**.

## Reproduction Steps

- Used the official script:
  ```bash
  python experiments/robot/libero/run_libero_eval.py \
    --model_family openvla \
    --pretrained_checkpoint openvla/openvla-7b-finetuned-libero-object \
    --task_suite_name libero_object \
    --center_crop True
  ```
- Dataset used: `libero_object_no_noops`

## What I Have Tried

- Changed random seed (`int seed = 3`, `int seed = 15`): success rate remains at 68%.
- Redownloaded the dataset via Huggingface: results unchanged.
- Increased `max_steps` to 300: slight improvement from 68% to 68.6%.
- Disabled flash-attention: improved by \~1% （68% -> 69%）.

[EVAL-libero_object-openvla-2025_07_15-19_45_24.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21336271/EVAL-libero_object-openvla-2025_07_15-19_45_24.txt)

## Environment

```
Python: 3.10.18 (main, Jun  5 2025, 13:14:17) [GCC 11.2.0]
Platform: Linux-6.8.0-60-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35
CUDA available: True
CUDA version: 12.1
cuDNN version: 8907
PyTorch version: 2.2.0+cu121
GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
Transformers version: 4.40.1
```

## Additional Information

- I have followed the official instructions, scripts, and used the recommended checkpoints.
- The large gap appears only on LIBERO-Object. The other benchmarks are close to the reported results.

**Is there anything I may have missed (dataset preprocessing, environment settings, etc.) that could explain this gap? Any advice for further debugging or pointers would be appreciated!**

Thanks!

        print("Target Orientation (quat w, x,y,z):", target_orientation_quat)

I also try to do that, integration works well, but arm makes stupid random movements and does not do anything meaningful

This is my code

```
import asyncio
import base64
import io
import os
import time

import numpy as np
import requests
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

import carb
import carb.settings
import omni.replicator.core as rep
import omni.kit.app
from omni.isaac.dynamic_control import _dynamic_control as dynamic_control
from omni.timeline import get_timeline_interface

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Config
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

OPENVLA_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8008/infer"
CAMERA_PATH = "/World/SceneCamera"
FRANKA_PATH = "/World/Franka"

# Put here your Render Resolution (Width, Height) from viewport
VIEW_RESOLUTION = (720, 720)  # ← поменяй под свои числа, если нужно

VLA_RESOLUTION = (224, 224)   # input size for OpenVLA

ACTION_SCALE = 0.2
FRAME_INTERVAL = 10           # do control step every N frames
MAX_STEPS = 200               # total OpenVLA steps before stopping

script_start_at = int(time.time())
print("=== OpenVLA control script v0_3_0, script_start_at =", script_start_at, "===")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

def get_img_dir():
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    img_dir = os.path.join(home, "lbm-kwargs")
    os.makedirs(img_dir, exist_ok=True)
    return img_dir


def make_images_with_crop(rgb_array: np.ndarray):
    """From Replicator rgb -> (hi_res_with_box, vla_res)."""

    if rgb_array.dtype != np.uint8:
        rgb_array = np.clip(rgb_array, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)

    if rgb_array.shape[-1] == 4:
        rgb_array = rgb_array[..., :3]

    img = Image.fromarray(rgb_array, "RGB")

    if img.size != VIEW_RESOLUTION:
        print("Warning: rgb size", img.size, "!= VIEW_RESOLUTION", VIEW_RESOLUTION)
        img = img.resize(VIEW_RESOLUTION, Image.BILINEAR)

    width, height = img.size
    side = min(width, height)

    left = (width - side) // 2
    top = (height - side) // 2
    right = left + side
    bottom = top + side

    crop_square = img.crop((left, top, right, bottom))
    img_vla = crop_square.resize(VLA_RESOLUTION, Image.BILINEAR)

    img_hi = img.copy()
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img_hi)
    thickness = 3
    for t in range(thickness):
        draw.rectangle(
            (left + t, top + t, right - t - 1, bottom - t - 1),
            outline=(255, 0, 0),
        )

    return img_hi, img_vla


def pil_to_jpeg_bytes(img: Image.Image, quality: int = 90) -> bytes:
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    img.save(buf, format="JPEG", quality=quality)
    return buf.getvalue()


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One control step (capture -> OpenVLA -> move)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

class OpenVLAController:
    def __init__(self):
        # enable capture on play so we can just read frames
        settings = carb.settings.get_settings()
        settings.set("/omni/replicator/captureOnPlay", True)

        # dynamic control
        self.dc = dynamic_control.acquire_dynamic_control_interface()
        self.art = self.dc.get_articulation(FRANKA_PATH)
        if not self.art:
            raise RuntimeError("Could not get articulation at path: %s" % FRANKA_PATH)

        self.dof_count = self.dc.get_articulation_dof_count(self.art)
        print("Franka DOF count:", self.dof_count)

        # replicator render product + annotator
        self.render_product = rep.create.render_product(CAMERA_PATH, VIEW_RESOLUTION)
        self.rgb_annot = rep.AnnotatorRegistry.get_annotator("rgb")
        self.rgb_annot.attach(self.render_product)

        self.img_dir = get_img_dir()
        self.step_idx = 0

    def read_joint_positions(self):
        joints = np.zeros(self.dof_count, dtype=np.float32)
        for i in range(self.dof_count):
            dof_h = self.dc.get_articulation_dof(self.art, i)
            joints[i] = self.dc.get_dof_position(dof_h)
        return joints

    def do_step(self):
        if self.step_idx >= MAX_STEPS:
            print("Reached MAX_STEPS =", MAX_STEPS, ", stopping control loop.")
            return False

        t0 = time.time()

        # read joints
        start_joints = self.read_joint_positions()

        # get latest rgb from replicator
        rgb_data = self.rgb_annot.get_data()
        if rgb_data is None:
            print("[step %d] rgb_data is None, skipping" % self.step_idx)
            return True

        img_hi, img_vla = make_images_with_crop(rgb_data)

        ts_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
        hi_name = "img_hi_%d_step%03d_%d.jpg" % (script_start_at, self.step_idx, ts_ms)
        vla_name = "img_vla_%d_step%03d_%d.jpg" % (script_start_at, self.step_idx, ts_ms)

        hi_path = os.path.join(self.img_dir, hi_name)
        vla_path = os.path.join(self.img_dir, vla_name)

        img_hi.save(hi_path, format="JPEG", quality=95)
        img_vla.save(vla_path, format="JPEG", quality=95)

        print("[step %d] saved hi-res:", hi_path)
        print("[step %d] saved vla-res:", vla_path)

        # send to OpenVLA
        jpeg_bytes = pil_to_jpeg_bytes(img_vla, quality=90)
        img_b64 = base64.b64encode(jpeg_bytes).decode("ascii")

        payload = {
            "image_b64": img_b64,
            "instruction": "pick up the red cube",
        }

        resp = requests.post(OPENVLA_URL, json=payload, timeout=60)
        resp.raise_for_status()
        data = resp.json()

        if "action" not in data:
            print("[step %d] response has no 'action' key: %s" % (self.step_idx, str(data)))
            return True

        action = np.array(data["action"], dtype=np.float32)
        if action.ndim == 2 and action.shape[0] == 1:
            action = action[0]

        n = min(len(action), self.dof_count)
        targets = start_joints.copy()
        targets[:n] += action[:n] * ACTION_SCALE

        delta = targets - start_joints
        delta_sum = float(delta.sum())
        delta_l2 = float(np.sqrt((delta ** 2).sum()))

        self.dc.set_articulation_dof_position_targets(self.art, targets)

        elapsed_ms = int((time.time() - t0) * 1000.0)
        print("[step %d] joints_start:", start_joints)
        print("[step %d] joints_target:", targets)
        print("[step %d] delta:", delta)
        print("[step %d] delta_sum: %.6f, delta_L2: %.6f" % (self.step_idx, delta_sum, delta_l2))
        print("[step %d] OpenVLA step time: %d ms" % (self.step_idx, elapsed_ms))

        self.step_idx += 1
        return True


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Subscription to per-frame updates
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

controller = OpenVLAController()
timeline = get_timeline_interface()
app = omni.kit.app.get_app()

state = {
    "frame": 0,
    "enabled": True,
}


def on_update(e):
    if not state["enabled"]:
        return

    if not timeline.is_playing():
        return

    state["frame"] += 1
    if state["frame"] % FRAME_INTERVAL != 0:
        return

    try:
        keep_going = controller.do_step()
        if not keep_going:
            state["enabled"] = False
            print("OpenVLA control loop finished (MAX_STEPS reached).")
    except Exception as exc:
        state["enabled"] = False
        print("OpenVLA control error:", repr(exc))


subscription = app.get_update_event_stream().create_subscription_to_pop(
    on_update, name="openvla_control_loop"
)

print("Subscribed OpenVLA control loop. It will run every", FRAME_INTERVAL, "frames.")
print("To stop it, restart Isaac Sim or set state['enabled'] = False in Script Editor.")
```

comments.author: lovecode1
comments.body:
The main goal in training or fine-tuning an AI model is to ensure it doesn’t memorize but rather generalizes. This way, even when it encounters a new angle or position, it can still determine the correct next move.

By switching camera positions and angles, enabling image augmentation, and adjusting other basic aspects of the scene, you force the model to learn the tasks regardless of its surroundings.

When all the training data is too similar, the model tends to memorize those details. As a result, when the environment changes even slightly, it may fail to respond correctly.

For example, if the model faces a move or an angle it has never seen before, and it is not generalized enough, it will not know what to do next.

comments.author: lovecode1
comments.body: You also need to ensure that the action data matches the robot’s coordinate system etc. and that there are no mismatches. Try running the training data actions directly on the robot to verify that it moves in the way you expect. This should be done even before any training takes place. It’s important to first confirm that the training data itself is correct.

comments.author: lovecode1
comments.body:
I think you’re missing the point of an AI model.
The goal is not to simply record a sequence of steps and replay them. Instead, you are training the AI to understand the concept of picking up an item and placing it in a different location.

Imagine if, for your entire life, you could only see the world from one fixed angle and position, with no ability to explore. Your knowledge would be extremely limited, and there would be many tasks you couldn’t complete.

In the same way, an AI model needs variety. Without variance, it will only memorize specific steps rather than learning the underlying concept.

comments.author: moojink
comments.body:
Hi @YY-GX,

For Diffusion Policy, we used the DROID policy learning repo here: https://github.com/droid-dataset/droid_policy_learning

The above is a language-conditioned version of the official Diffusion Policy implementation here: https://github.com/real-stanford/diffusion_policy

We unfortunately do not plan to release code/checkpoints for baseline methods but can provide some details that may be helpful. For Diffusion Policy on LIBERO, here are some details:
* Trained for 25-50 epochs per task suite independently
* Batch size 128
* 2-step observation history, 8-step prediction horizon with 3-step action horizon (i.e., predict 8 actions and execute 3)
* DDIM sampler with 100 diffusion steps
* 224x224 px images (third-person only) + robot proprio state as input
* Image augmentations: Color jitter + random crop (with 202x202 px crops)

-Moo Jin

> * Batch size 128

> * DDIM sampler with 100 diffusion steps
> * 224x224 px images (third-person only) + robot proprio state as input
> * Image augmentations: Color jitter + random crop (with 202x202 px crops)
> 
> -Moo Jin

body:
**Hardware:** Lambda Labs GH200 (ARM64, H100, CUDA 12.3, PyTorch 2.2)
**Config:** LoRA rank=32, LR=5e-4, batch=16, 10k steps on `libero_spatial_no_noops`
**Base model:** `openvla/openvla-7b`

## Results

| Model | Eval (LIBERO-Spatial, 10 tasks × 5 trials) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `openvla/openvla-7b-finetuned-libero-spatial` (authors' checkpoint) | **37/50 = 74%** | Paper reports 84.7% on x86; gap likely due to flash-attn not installed (pre-built wheel in NVIDIA container is x86-only; we did not compile from source) |
| Our LoRA fine-tune (base model + `finetune.py`, 10k steps) | **0/50 = 0%** | Mode collapse — identical action tokens every step regardless of observation |

Both models evaluated on the **exact same hardware and setup**, confirming the eval environment is not the issue.

## Training curves (W&B)

![Training curves](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shant0602/PhysicalAI/feature/openvla-training-pipeline/assets/training_curves_run1.png)

**Key observations:**
- Loss spike at step ~6000: jumps from ~2.2 → ~5.2
- Action accuracy crashes to near 0 at the same step and never recovers
- Final action accuracy: 0.39 (expected ~0.90+)

## Symptoms

- `action_accuracy` reaches only ~0.39 at 10k steps (expected ~0.9+)
- `train_loss` never meaningfully converges
- At inference, model outputs **identical action tokens every step regardless of image input** — mode collapse

## Hypothesis

`finetune.py` uses raw AdamW with no gradient clipping. A single outlier batch can produce an unclamped gradient that corrupts the LoRA weights. Standard transformer fine-tuning (LLaMA, PrismaticVLM, etc.) uses `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, max_norm=1.0)` before the optimizer step — this is absent from `finetune.py`.

Note: multiple other users have reported the same 0% success rate symptom in #299 (open since Sep 2025, no fix yet).

## Question

Was gradient clipping used in the internal training pipeline for the published LIBERO checkpoints? If so, would you accept a PR adding it to `finetune.py`?

## Proposed fix (one line)

```python
# Around line 316 of vla-scripts/finetune.py, before optimizer.step():
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(trainable_params, max_norm=1.0)
optimizer.step()
```

comments.author: shant0602
comments.body:
cc @moojink @kpertsch — posting results in case this is useful for the repo.

**Update: fix confirmed with experimental results — PR #334**

We ran two training runs on the same hardware (GH200, ARM64, CUDA 12.3) to isolate the effect of gradient clipping.

### Training runs comparison

| | Run 1 (original) | Run 2 (with fix) |
|---|---|---|
| Gradient clipping | No | Yes |
| Start checkpoint | openvla/openvla-7b | openvla/openvla-7b |
| Steps | 10k | 20k (two sequential 10k runs, second resumed from run 1's merged checkpoint) |
| Batch size | 16 | 16 |
| LoRA rank | 32 | 32 |
| Learning rate | 5e-4 | 5e-4 |
| Final train loss | 2.66 | 0.68 |
| Final action acc (training) | 0.39 | 0.82 |
| Loss spike? | Yes (~step 6k, 2.2 → 5.2) | No |

### LIBERO-Spatial evaluation (10 tasks × 5 trials = 50 episodes)

| Checkpoint | Steps | Score (50 eps) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openvla/openvla-7b-finetuned-libero-spatial` (authors') | 10k | 37/50 = 74% | Baseline on same ARM64 hardware |
| Run 1 — no clipping | 10k | 0/50 = 0% | Mode collapse — identical action tokens at inference regardless of observation |
| **Run 2 — with clipping** | **20k** | **36/50 = 72%** | Merged checkpoint, public on HF (note: 2× the training budget of the official checkpoint) |

### Training curves — before and after

| ✗ Run 1 — no gradient clipping (10k steps) | ✓ Run 2 — with gradient clipping (20k steps) |
|---|---|
| ![Run 1 loss spike](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shant0602/PhysicalAI/feature/openvla-training-pipeline/assets/training_curves_run1.png) | ![Run 2 clean convergence](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shant0602/PhysicalAI/feature/openvla-training-pipeline/assets/training_curves_20k.png) |
| Loss spikes at step ~6k, accuracy collapses to 0 and never recovers | Loss decreases steadily 2.4 → 0.68, accuracy rises 0.05 → 0.82 — no spike |

### Notes on the gap vs. paper (84.7%)

| Factor | Our setup | Paper setup |
|---|---|---|
| Hardware | GH200, ARM64 | x86 |
| flash-attn | Built from source (2.5.8) | Pre-built wheel |
| Official checkpoint eval on our hardware | 74% | 84.7% (paper) |

The ~12pp gap is consistent with the hardware difference — the official checkpoint also scores 74% (not 84.7%) on our ARM64 setup, suggesting hardware is the primary driver of the gap rather than training quality.

### Artifacts

| | Link |
|---|---|
| PR with one-line fix | https://github.com/openvla/openvla/pull/334 |
| 20k checkpoint (public, merged weights) | https://huggingface.co/shant0602/openvla-7b-libero-spatial-lora-20k |

comments.author: rylinjames
comments.body: your hypothesis is almost certainly right. the loss spike at step ~6000 jumping 2.2→5.2 with action accuracy crashing to ~0 is textbook unclipped gradient blowup on lora, especially at lr=5e-4 rank=32 which is on the aggressive side. adding `torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, max_norm=1.0)` before `optimizer.step()` in finetune.py should fix it, and dropping lr to 2e-4 as a belt-and-suspenders. also worth enabling bf16 instead of fp16 if you're on gh200 (hopper), fp16 on libero has a history of flaky lora. reflex doesn't cover openvla training (we focus on deploy for smolvla/pi0/pi0.5/gr00t), so this isn't our layer, but if you end up with a working lora checkpoint and want onnx + trt deploy, we export with cos=+1.0 parity. github.com/rylinjames/reflex-vla has good-first-issues, or dm romirj on discord / playindus@gmail.com for collaborator access.

body:
I’ve identified an inconsistency in how the VLA model’s output actions are interpreted across the Libero and Simpler test environments, particularly with respect to angle representations:

1. In the Libero test (see experiments/robot/libero/run_libero_eval.py ), the angle information from the VLA model’s output action is interpreted as an axis-angle representation. Upon reviewing the Libero environment code, I couldn’t locate any explicit conversion logic (e.g., from axis-angle to Euler angles or vice versa) that would explain this. However, in the robosuite codebase, I found that the robot directly sets the goal orientation based on the action, where the action is interpreted as the desired relative change in orientation in axis-angle form [ax, ay, az]. This is evident in robosuite/utils/control_utils.py in the set_goal_orientation function:

2. In the Simpler test (experiments/robot/simpler/run_simpler_eval.py), the same angle information from the VLA model’s output is interpreted as Euler angles. These are then converted to axis-angle form using the euler2axangle function in convert_maniskill before being passed to env.step. This can be seen in the line:

`obs, reward, done, trunc, info = env.step(convert_maniskill(action))`

This discrepancy raises several questions:

1. Is this inconsistency in angle interpretation (axis-angle in Libero vs. Euler angles in Simpler) intentional, or could it be a bug? if I need to evaluate the vla model in libero, I need to finetune the vla with data in axis-angle form?
2. If intentional, where exactly is the conversion between axis-angle and Euler angles handled in the codebase? I might have overlooked the relevant logic. I am sorry for my careless mistake.
3. If unintentional, could this inconsistency impact the VLA model’s performance consistency across the two test environments?

I’d greatly appreciate clarification on how angle representations are managed in this project and whether this behavior is expected. If there’s a specific part of the code or documentation I should review to better understand this, please point me in the right direction!

Steps to Reproduce:

Run the VLA model evaluation in the Libero test environment (experiments/robot/libero/run_libero_eval.py) and inspect the angle component of the action output.
Run the same model in the Simpler test environment (experiments/robot/simpler/run_simpler_eval.py) and compare the angle interpretation.
Check the Libero environment code and robosuite/utils/control_utils.py for axis-angle usage, and convert_maniskill in the Simpler pipeline for Euler-to-axis-angle conversion.
Expected Behavior:
The angle representation from the VLA model’s output should be consistently interpreted (e.g., either axis-angle or Euler angles) across both test environments, or there should be explicit conversion logic documented in the codebase to handle the differences.

Actual Behavior:

In Libero: Angles are interpreted as axis-angle with no visible conversion in the environment code.
In Simpler: Angles are interpreted as Euler angles and converted to axis-angle via euler2axangle before env.step.

I just use the provided finetuned script with the hyperparameters listed in https://huggingface.co/openvla/openvla-7b-finetuned-libero-spatial#openvla-7b-fine-tuned-on-libero-spatial.

Here's the training script

```shell
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 torchrun --standalone --nnodes 1 --nproc-per-node 4 vla-scripts/finetune.py \
  --vla_path "openvla/openvla-7b" \
  --data_root_dir datasets/open-x-embodiment \
  --dataset_name libero_spatial_no_noops \
  --lora_rank 32 \
  --batch_size 6 \
  --grad_accumulation_steps 1 \
  --learning_rate 5e-4 \
  --image_aug True \
  --save_steps 2000 \
  --max_steps 50000
```

And the evaluation script
```
python experiments/robot/libero/run_libero_eval.py  --model_family openvla  --pretrained_checkpoint outputs/openvla-7b+libero_spatial_no_noops+b6+lr-0.0005+lora-r32+dropout-0.0--image_aug  --task_suite_name libero_spatial --center_crop True
```

As a result, I only get a performance of 79.0%, which is lower than the reported 84.7%.

comments.author: kpertsch
comments.body:
Hi! Thanks for your questions.
Indeed, you need to register new datasets in the files you mentioned -- we should document this better!
Re unnorm_key: this is an unresolved issue -- the HF automodel does not have the new datasets_statistics in the finetuning stage, so indeed I have loaded them manually from the file for finetuned models so far.

Regarding your performance questions:
- I would recommend storing images at a higher resolution (eg 256) and then let our model downsize them to 224, rather than making them smaller to start with
- it is really important that your inference pipeline mirrors exactly all preprocessing steps you did for going from raw RLBench data to model inputs. this includes any resizes (make sure to also match the resize method) -- esp for sim data with very little variation, small artifacts of resizing can really throw policies off
- re camera view: I would suggest you start with a third-person view and see whether the model behaves more reasonably -- OpenVLA was only trained with 3rd person views, and the distribution shift to a wrist view would be quite large.
- we usually use image_aug for real world finetuning, but in sim it may not be that important since the eval scene camera viewpoint / lighting match training exactly

comments.body:
Same issue here — LoRA fine-tune on `libero_spatial_no_noops`, 10k steps, batch=16, LR=5e-4, 0% eval success with mode collapse (identical action tokens every step regardless of observation).

We verified the **eval environment is not the problem**: tested `openvla/openvla-7b-finetuned-libero-spatial` on the exact same setup (ARM64/GH200, osmesa, all patches) and got ~75% task success, consistent with the paper. So the issue is isolated to training.

Our hypothesis and full details: #333

The `v-xchen-v` finding about LR reduction is interesting — may be related to effective LR scaling, or may interact with the missing `clip_grad_norm_` in the optimizer step.

comments.author: shant0602
comments.body:
**Root cause identified and fixed — see PR #334**

Following up on my earlier comment: the root cause is confirmed. `vla-scripts/finetune.py` is missing `clip_grad_norm_` before `optimizer.step()`. A single outlier batch produces an unclamped gradient large enough to permanently corrupt the LoRA weights.

**Fix (one line, PR #334):**
```python
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(trainable_params, max_norm=1.0)
optimizer.step()
```

**Results with fix applied (LIBERO-Spatial, 10 tasks × 5 trials):**

| | Without fix | With fix |
|---|---|---|
| Train loss (10k steps) | 2.66 (spike at step ~6k) | converges cleanly |
| Action acc (training) | 0.39 | 0.82 (at 20k steps) |
| LIBERO-Spatial eval | 0% (mode collapse) | **72%** |

Full analysis and loss curves: #333
One-line PR: #334
Public 20k checkpoint: https://huggingface.co/shant0602/openvla-7b-libero-spatial-lora-20k

comments.author: moojink
comments.body:
Hi @ClousTom,

You can still use `ActionEncoding.JOINT_POS` it if you comment out or modify the assert statement here: https://github.com/openvla/openvla/blob/0214a0c7c09942fb8e0ec3c3948c00e4e8949911/prismatic/vla/datasets/rlds/oxe/materialize.py#L33

We just added that assert statement to catch the potential mistake of using the wrong action representation for OpenVLA, since for all the OpenX datasets we were pretraining with, we used the `ActionEncoding.EEF_POS` representation.

You might observe less positive transfer using `ActionEncoding.JOINT_POS` given we didn't pretrain OpenVLA using it, but it should still work if you fine-tune the model!

body:
Hi, I noticed that in the base prompter used for training, https://github.com/openvla/openvla/blob/7a359de9bb8be6fd3c232d189784920dbc93391c/prismatic/models/backbones/llm/prompting/base_prompter.py#L36
there is a space at the end of `Out`, however, all the examples for inference, such as https://github.com/openvla/openvla/blob/7a359de9bb8be6fd3c232d189784920dbc93391c/experiments/robot/openvla_utils.py#L163
seem to remove that space, what's the reasoning behind this discrepancy? Shouldn't we want the prompt to be identical between training and inference?

comments.author: moojink
comments.body:
Hi @oceanusxiv,

Thank you for the question!

**TLDR:** It turns out everything works fine and there is no discrepancy between train time and test time if you run the inference code as is, because the OpenVLA `predict_action()` function adds a special empty token to the end of the prompt, before the action tokens are predicted, to resolve the discrepancy.

----

**Detailed explanation:**

Consider an example where the task is to `"pick up the black bowl next to the ramekin and place it on the plate"`. Then, the prompt and response at train time would be the following (excluding the image for simplicity):

`"<s>In: What action should the robot take to pick up the black bowl next to the ramekin and place it on the plate?\nOut: ABCDEFG</s>"`,

where `ABCDEFG` denote the 7 robot action tokens OpenVLA needs to predict. (These are just symbols -- not the literal tokens. The real tokens might look something like `貴학 ਿ˚陈 ਿ忠`, which come from the set of last 256 tokens in the vocabulary.)

OpenVLA's tokenization of the above produces the following `input_ids`:

`[1, 512, 29901, 1724, 3158, 881, 278, 19964, 2125, 304, 5839, 701, 278, 4628, 12580, 29880, 2446, 304, 278, 364, 420, 9089, 322, 2058, 372, 373, 278, 15284, 29973, 13, 3744, 29901, 29871, 31887, 31822, 31857, 31878, 31862, 31857, 31744, 2]`

You can use the tokenizer to decode the `input_ids` into individual tokens like so:

```
id: 1           token: <s>
id: 512         token: In
id: 29901       token: :
id: 1724        token: What
id: 3158        token: action
id: 881         token: should
id: 278         token: the
id: 19964       token: robot
id: 2125        token: take
id: 304         token: to
id: 5839        token: pick
id: 701         token: up
id: 278         token: the
id: 4628        token: black
id: 12580       token: bow
id: 29880       token: l
id: 2446        token: next
id: 304         token: to
id: 278         token: the
id: 364         token: r
id: 420         token: ame
id: 9089        token: kin
id: 322         token: and
id: 2058        token: place
id: 372         token: it
id: 373         token: on
id: 278         token: the
id: 15284       token: plate
id: 29973       token: ?
id: 13          token: <NEWLINE>
id: 3744        token: Out
id: 29901       token: :
id: 29871       token: 
id: 31887       token: 貴
id: 31822       token: 학
id: 31857       token: ਿ
id: 31878       token: ˚
id: 31862       token: 陈
id: 31857       token: ਿ
id: 31744       token: 忠
id: 2           token: </s>
```

At test time, if you use the prompt `f"In: What action should the robot take to {task_label.lower()}?\nOut:"` with no space character at the end and then break it down into individual tokens like above, then you will see that the `input_ids` looks the same as above, except that the token with ID `29871` (representing the empty `''` token) is missing. At first glance, this may appear to be a problem, but the OpenVLA `predict_action()` function actually handles this by adding the empty token to the prompt, as shown [here](https://huggingface.co/openvla/openvla-7b/blob/main/modeling_prismatic.py#L513). Therefore, there is no discrepancy between train and test time.

If you change the prompt and add a space character (i.e., use `"Out: "` instead of `"Out:"`), that's still fine because `predict_action()` performs a check and doesn't add the empty token if it already exists at the end of the prompt, as shown [here](https://huggingface.co/openvla/openvla-7b/blob/main/modeling_prismatic.py#L512).
* **[Note (2024-09-16)]:** We added this check to the public GitHub repo some time in the past, as shown in [this commit](https://github.com/openvla/openvla/commit/d7dbea892e0772716f198c31fb1a1da24f4bb129), but recently realized that the change wasn't reflected in the Hugging Face OpenVLA inference code that is downloaded to cache along with the model checkpoint. Therefore, we just updated the Hugging Face code today to match the GitHub repo (you can clear your Hugging Face OpenVLA cache to see the changes locally). However, this should not have caused any issues if you used the inference code exactly as shown in `openvla_utils.py`.

Hope that helps clears things up!

-Moo Jin

comments.author: oceanusxiv
moojink
comments.body:
Hi @oceanusxiv,

1. Thank you for pointing that out in `openvla.py`! We just pushed a [commit](https://github.com/openvla/openvla/commit/c40d1ffa6f673d08ef36dbaa123425e9638e0b7a) to address that.
2. Good point. At some point we did have code to handle cases like that but refactored it away since we didn't end up developing OpenVLA with different base LLMs and we didn't want the code to be too clunky or confusing to people. But yes, customizing the model like that will require tweaking the `predict_action()` function definition!

-Moo Jin

comments.author: kpertsch
comments.body:
Hi!
To confirm: did you train your model to predict a single action at a time or an action chunk? The repeating action problem can be quite common for action chunks, but I would be surprised if it's common for single action prediction with various inputs.

If you want to debug this, a simple step would be to load up some images from the training data in your inference pipeline and pretend that they came from the robot camera. If everything is set up correctly the model should output the correct actions from the training data for the training images.

title: About LIBERO configs and transforms

body:
## Problem

`vla-scripts/finetune.py` applies AdamW updates with no gradient norm clipping. A single outlier batch can produce an unclamped gradient large enough to permanently corrupt the LoRA weights — causing a loss spike and mode collapse that the training run never recovers from.

Observed on LIBERO-Spatial (`libero_spatial_no_noops`), GH200 / ARM64, LoRA rank=32, LR=5e-4:

- Without the fix: loss spike at step ~6k (2.2 → 5.2), action accuracy collapses to ~0 and stays there. Inference produces identical action tokens regardless of the observation (mode collapse). Eval: **0% on LIBERO-Spatial**.
- With the fix: clean convergence, no spike. Eval: **56% at 10k steps**, **72% at 20k steps**.

Full analysis, loss curves, and three-run ablation in issue #333.

## Fix

One line, before `optimizer.step()`:

```python
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(trainable_params, max_norm=1.0)
```

`max_norm=1.0` is the standard value used in LLaMA, PrismaticVLM, and most transformer fine-tuning recipes.

## Evidence

| Run | Steps | Train loss | Action acc | LIBERO-Spatial eval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No clipping (original) | 10k | 2.66 | 0.39 | 0% (mode collapse) |
| With clipping | 10k | 1.27 | 0.56 | 56% |
| With clipping (continued) | 20k total | 0.68 | 0.82 | 72% |

Trained checkpoint (20k steps, public): https://huggingface.co/shant0602/openvla-7b-libero-spatial-lora-20k

Closes #333
